title: Memperkenalkan Label Baru untuk Identitas Artis Buatan AI di Spotify
summary: Koneksi antara artis dan fans yang sesungguhnya hanya dapat terbagun dengan landasan kepercayaan dan autentisitas. Dalam dunia musik, ini berarti pendengar harus bisa percaya bahwa artis di balik musik yang mereka dengarkan benar-benar sesuai dengan yang ditampilkan. Hal ini menjadi semakin penting di era AI generatif. Oleh karena itu, tahun ini kami menjadikan Identitas &...
body_text: Koneksi antara artis dan fans yang sesungguhnya hanya dapat terbagun dengan landasan kepercayaan dan autentisitas. Dalam dunia musik, ini berarti pendengar harus bisa percaya bahwa artis di balik musik yang mereka dengarkan benar-benar sesuai dengan yang ditampilkan. Hal ini menjadi semakin penting di era AI generatif. Oleh karena itu, tahun ini kami menjadikan Identitas & Kepercayaan Artis sebagai salah satu prioritas utama kami melalui peluncuran Verified by Spotify , SongDNA , AI Credits, dan Artist Profile Protection . Hari ini, kami mengumumkan langkah berikutnya dalam upaya kami memastikan Spotify menjadi platform paling transparan dan terpercaya untuk mendengarkan musik. Pendengar telah menyampaikan dengan jelas bahwa mereka merasa tidak nyaman ketika melihat profil artis yang tampak seperti manusia sungguhan, namun ternyata persona tersebut dibuat oleh AI. Karena itu, mulai pertengahan September, Anda akan mulai melihat lencana AI Persona di beberapa profil artis. Lencana ini memberi sinyal kepada pendengar bahwa identitas artis tersebut kemungkinan dibuat oleh AI dan tidak merepresentasikan orang sungguhan. Selain profil artis yang secara terbuka menyatakan diri sebagai AI Persona, kami juga akan mulai memberikan lencana ini pada profil lain yang relevan berdasarkan hasil tinjauan kami. Pada dasarnya, Spotify tidak akan menyertakan AI Persona dalam rekomendasi editorial maupun algoritmik . Artinya, Anda tidak akan melihat musik dari AI Persona direkomendasi yang dipersonalisasi untuk Anda, kecuali jika Anda memang mengikuti AI Persona tersebut. Meskipun kami percaya semua artis memiliki kebebasan kreatif dalam menentukan cara mereka menampilkan diri, pemrograman Spotify berfokus untuk mengangkat musik dari artis autentik yang sedang membangun karier di dunia musik. Cara Kerja Label AI Persona Mulai hari ini, artis dapat menyatakan bahwa profil mereka merepresentasikan AI Persona melalui Spotify for Artists . Kami berharap artis bersikap transparan, sehingga kami memberikan kesempatan untuk pengungkapan diri secara mandiri ( self disclosure ). Namun kami tidak akan hanya bergantung pada pengungkapan mandiri saja. Spotify juga akan meninjau profil artis dan mengidentifikasi profil yang identitas publiknya —yaitu identitas yang ditampilkan di profil mereka, termasuk nama dan gambar—tampak merepresentasikan identitas fotorealistik yang dibuat oleh AI. Kami akan memulai dari artis yang telah mencapai ambang batas audiens tertentu, sehingga lencana ini mencakup sebagian besar profil artis yang dikunjungi pengguna. Pada pertengahan September , Anda akan mulai melihat lencana AI Persona muncul di profil artis (di banner dan bagian Tentang), di Pencarian, serta pada baris lagu di berbagai playlist. Saat pendengar mengetuk lencana tersebut, mereka dapat melihat apakah artis tersebut secara transparan menyatakan diri sebagai AI Persona sebagai upaya untuk membangun kepercayaan dengan calon pendengar, atau apakah Spotify yang melakukan tinjauan dan menetapkannya berdasarkan informasi yang tersedia. Untuk profil artis yang telah diberi label oleh tim peninjau Spotify, artis terkait akan menerima pemberitahuan dan kesempatan untuk mengungkapkan diri secara mandiri ( self-disclose ) atau mengajukan banding. Dalam beberapa bulan mendatang, kami juga akan memberikan opsi bagi pendengar untuk melaporkan profil artis yang mereka yakini merepresentasikan AI Persona kepada tim peninjau kami. Kami akan membagikan informasi lebih lanjut saat fitur ini tersedia. Meskipun terdapat spektrum yang begitu luas ketika berbicara tentang bagaimana cara artis menggunakan Akal Imitasi (AI) sebagai alat kreatif, Spotify dapat membantu memberikan kejelasan dalam menentukan apakah sebuah profil merepresentasikan manusia sungguhan atau bukan. Lencana ini berkaitan dengan identitas publik artis, bukan tentang cara musiknya dibuat. Untuk informasi lebih lanjut tentang cara pembuatan musik, kami menyediakan AI Credits dan SongDNA . Melalui AI Credits, kami telah melihat antusiasme dan menggunakan kesempatan tersebut untuk secara transparan berbagi tentang bagaimana mereka menggunakan AI sebagai bagian dari proses kreatif lagu mereka. Kami berharap tingkat pengungkapan yang serupa untuk AI Persona. Membangun kepercayaan dan transparansi di Spotify Lencana AI Persona adalah bagian dari upaya kami yang lebih luas untuk menjadikan Spotify sebagai platform paling transparan dan terpercaya untuk mendengarkan musik. Pada tahun 2026, kami telah memperkenalkan beberapa fitur lain yang dirancang untuk memberikan transparansi lebih kepada pendengar tentang apa yang mereka dengarkan dan siapa sosok di baliknya: Verified by Spotify memberi sinyal kepada pendengar bahwa seorang artis adalah manusia sungguhan yang menampilkan diri secara autentik di platform. Ratusan ribu profil telah terverifikasi, mayoritas di antaranya adalah artis independen, yang merepresentasikan lebih dari 99% artis yang aktif dicari pendengar Spotify. AI Credits memungkinkan artis mengungkapkan kepada pendengar bagaimana mereka menggunakan AI dalam proses pembuatan musik. Setiap harinya, ada puluhan ribu kredit AI yang diajukan. SongDNA memberikan konteks lebih mendalam kepada pendengar tentang artis dan kontributor di balik sebuah lagu, membantu mereka menemukan dan jatuh cinta dengan sosok di balik proses kreatifnya. Artist Details menampilkan informasi artis berdasarkan data platform yang dimiliki Spotify, seperti pencapaian karier, riwayat rilis, dan aktivitas tur yang memberikan gambaran singkat tentang aktivitas autentik seorang artis di Spotify. Artist Profile Protection memungkinkan artis meninjau dan menyetujui rilis yang dikirimkan ke Spotify untuk melindungi identitas artis mereka dan mencegah kebingungan pendengar akibat musik yang salah atribusi. Selain fitur-fitur tersebut, kami juga menyempurnakan algoritma kami untuk mengutamakan artis manusia yang autentik. Berdasarkan sinyal yang tersedia, kami berupaya untuk tidak menyertakan spam , konten asal-asalan ( slop ), atau konten berkualitas rendah dalam rekomendasi kami. Kami memahami bahwa ekosistem musik terus berkembang, begitu pula dengan pendekatan kami. Kami akan terus beradaptasi seiring perubahan lanskap industri dan seiring kami belajar dari para artis, pendengar, serta mitra industri.

title: Almost Half of Malware Samples Communicate Direct to IP
summary: Nearly half of C2 malware bypasses DNS by connecting directly to IP addresses. Zero trust IP enforcement secures networks against these threats.
body_text: Executive Summary Malware samples often bypass DNS entirely, communicating directly to IP addresses instead. Our analysis of 4 million dynamic analysis reports indicates that almost half (45.32%) of malware samples with any command-and-control (C2) activity made at least one direct-to-IP (D2IP) address connection. Measured as a fraction of all C2 connection attempts, D2IP traffic accounts for 23.17% of the total. A wide variety of threats — including ransomware droppers, peer-to-peer (P2P) botnets and supply chain risks — communicate directly with hard-coded IP addresses, bypassing DNS entirely and evading DNS-based defenses altogether. This article introduces zero trust IP (ZT-IP), which is a network-level enforcement approach that applies zero trust principles to IP-based traffic. The enforcement approach verifies whether outbound connection destinations were ever sanctioned by a DNS response. We validate this approach against real-world network traffic and samples, demonstrating how ZT-IP successfully surfaces threats including: Phorpiex ransomware droppers connecting directly to C2 IP addresses A persistent data exfiltration campaign using a custom obfuscated HTTP GET request Mozi P2P botnet payloads delivered to internet-of-things (IoT) devices without DNS Palo Alto Networks customers are better protected from the threats discussed here through the following products and services: Advanced WildFire Advanced URL Filtering and Advanced DNS Security Cortex XDR and XSIAM If you think you might have been compromised or have an urgent matter, contact the Unit 42 Incident Response team . Related Unit 42 Topics Malware , DNS , Ransomware The DNS Visibility Gap DNS security has become a cornerstone of enterprise threat defense. By monitoring and filtering DNS queries, security teams can block malware from reaching known-bad domains and use sinkholing to disrupt C2 communications before they establish a foothold. This approach is effective when malware plays by the rules of relying on DNS for domain resolution. However, many types of malware do not. For example, a backdoor malware sample made no DNS query at all before initiating a WebSocket connection directly to an IP address. Disassembly via Ghidra revealed why. The destination address wss://154.92.19[.]71:39989 was hard coded into the binary as a Unicode string. This is not an isolated edge case. Without the DNS resolution step in network communications, malware is invisible to DNS-based security controls, protective DNS sinkholing and DNS anomaly detection systems. The connection simply appears as raw IP traffic with no prior context. Prevalence of IP Traffic in Malware We analyzed over 4 million Advanced WildFire dynamic analysis reports for a 30-day period to quantify how prevalent this behavior truly is. We filtered out connections to common legitimate services, internal addresses and DNS resolvers. After doing that, we found that 20.11% of malware samples exhibited C2 activity. The contrast with benign samples is striking. Only 1% of benign samples establish connections to untrusted IP addresses after applying the same filtering criteria. Those that do average just 1.6 such connections per sample. This is a small fraction of the activity observed in malware. Among malware with C2 connections, TCP dominates (94.43% prevalence, averaging 4.17 unique C2 IP addresses per sample). UDP is present in 17.50% of cases but contacts far more IP addresses per sample (average 13.79%), consistent with scanning and P2P mesh behavior. Most critically for DNS-based defenses, 45.32% of malware samples with any C2 activity made at least one direct-to-IP (D2IP) address connection — a raw IP contact with no preceding DNS query. Even after excluding bulk port-scanning behavior, the figure remains 41.97%. Measured as a fraction of all C2 connection attempts, D2IP traffic accounts for 23.17% of the total. Threats Discovered Through ZT-IP Analysis By searching for D2IP connections (ZT-IP analysis), we were able to uncover multiple threats. Phorpiex Ransomware Dropper Among traffic flagged by ZT-IP, we observed the following suspicious HTTP GET request toward the destination IP address at 178.16.54[.]109 as shown below in Figure 1. Figure 1. Suspicious HTTP GET request to 178.16.54[.]109 . The observed request exhibits multiple variations, including sequential numeric GET paths (e.g., /1 through /6 ) and specific file downloads (e.g., /sex/k/n.txt , /new.php ). We found that these requests correlate with several malware samples (e.g., the binary retrieved from hxxp[:]//178.16.54[.]109/st.exe ) associated with Phorpiex (aka Trik), a long-running malware family used primarily as a dropper and spam botnet. Figure 2 illustrates the many malicious samples hosted on 178.16.54[.]109 in a flow chart of this activity. Figure 2. The IP address 178.16.54[.]109 is used to deliver multiple threats.This traffic aligns with Phorpiex's staged payload delivery mechanism. This mechanism is characterized by initially fetching configuration, and then retrieving additional malicious components such as a ransomware payload. A key indicator of malicious D2IP activity was the absence of DNS queries preceding the connections to 178.16.54[.]109 . Since the request bodies appear benign, they often bypass standard heuristic detectors. The \GET Exfiltration Campaign One of the most distinctive findings was a persistent campaign using a non-standard HTTP request we call the \GET protocol. This is an obfuscated request format designed to evade security detection while exfiltrating data. Unlike standard HTTP requests, these requests begin with \GET (backslash- GET ) rather than standard GET followed by a backslash. The \GET is followed by a long encoded string ranging from 250–666 characters, as shown in Figure 3. Figure 3. \GET protocol request to 18.228.188[.]56 .Statistical analysis of the encoded payloads reveals a structured encoding scheme: The first and last four characters: alphanumeric ( 0-9 and A-Z ), evenly distributed Middle characters: hex-like ( 0-9 and A-F ), evenly distributed The payload length ranges from 250–666 characters Disassembly of associated malware samples (e.g., cc43cdbe8eb9874f55fffbe23b560b673eb9f31fb9a953926bba29464fd2dd07 ) confirms there are no hex-format IP addresses hard coded in the binaries. Instead, multiple hard-coded strings follow the same encoding rule, consistent with the payload lengths observed. The C2 infrastructure is hosted on public cloud infrastructure in Brazil. Samples that point to it were found impacting high-value sectors including government, airlines and universities. Because the threat leverages shared cloud resources, simple IP-based blocking is ineffective. Furthermore, the malware employs a notable operational security measure. It rotates both its destination port and IP address on a regular schedule, which evades static IP-blocking defenses. SectopRAT We observed two separate attackers operating infrastructure at 87.120.107[.]33 and 194.76.227[.]94 , respectively, deploying the same malware family of SectopRAT against educational institutions. Both actors leverage SectopRAT's in-browser proxy capability to silently mirror all victim browser traffic to attacker-controlled servers in real time. The proxy operates via two endpoints. The first, /churl (shown in Figure 4), relays every URL the victim visits, including: Authenticated session pages Single sign-on (SSO) redirects Learning management system content Figure 4. HTTP GET request using /churl . The second, /fsave (shown in Figure 5), exfiltrates form fields including usernames and plaintext passwords at the moment of submission. Figure 5. HTTP GET request using /fsave . An identifier ( pcid/clid ) in every request allows each actor to track individual compromised devices across sessions. Both attackers’ campaigns communicate entirely over D2IP connections, bypassing DNS-based visibility layers entirely. IoT Botnets IoT malware families often exploit network vulnerabilities to self-propagate, relying on D2IP communication that makes them invisible to DNS-based security layers. Mozi is a Mirai-derived P2P botnet known for targeting IoT devices with MIPS, ARM and x86 architectures. We observed its characteristic exploitation payload embedded directly in HTTP requests. Figure 6 shows an example of the exploitation payload for Mozi. Figure 6. Example of an IoT exploitation payload embedded in an HTTP request. In ASCII text, this translates to the three commands shown in Figure 7. Figure 7. Commands from the IoT exploitation, listed in sequential order. The Mozi campaign showed highly distributed patterns with thousands of source and destination IP addresses, consistent with the Mozi botnet's P2P mesh structure. However, because this IoT malware propagates by making D2IP connections without DNS resolution, blocking this type of connection can effectively prevent it from spreading within sensitive environments. Similarly, we identified a Mirai variant that we named Boatnet, which was distributed from the IP address 2.26.98[.]67 . Boatnet demonstrates thorough platform targeting, covering at least 14 different architectures. Beyond standard IoT architectures, Boatnet includes binaries for m68k (Motorola 68000). This processor family is common in legacy industrial control systems (ICS) and aging embedded hardware, which current malware typically overlooks. Unlike generic variants, Boatnet fragments its ARM coverage into three discrete sub-variants (ARM5, ARM6 and ARM7) to ensure optimal performance across different hardware generations. Binaries are hosted under a /hiddenbin/ directory, as noted in Figure 8, showing a deliberate attempt to mimic legitimate system paths and evade basic file-path detection. Figure 8. HTTP GET request showing a Boatnet binary under a /hiddenbin/ directory. We observed infected devices fetching payloads with a User-Agent string of Wget/1.13.4 (released in 2012). This serves as a significant fingerprint, suggesting the botnet is specifically harvesting older, unpatched hardware. Boatnet also demonstrates more operational maturity than “vanilla” Mirai through its use of HTTP Range headers. Conclusion D2IP communication from malware won’t be detected by approaches that focus specifically on securing requests at the time a hostname is resolved. This is illustrated by threats like the Phorpiex ransomware dropper, the obfuscated \GET exfiltration campaign and the P2P Mozi botnet. ZT-IP closes this critical gap by applying strict zero trust principles to outbound D2IP connections, ensuring only DNS-sanctioned traffic is permitted. It is a necessary network-level enforcement mechanism to block what DNS-based detection cannot see. Palo Alto Networks customers are better protected from the threats discussed here through the following products and services: Advanced WildFire machine-learning models and analysis techniques have been reviewed and updated in light of the IoCs shared in this research. Advanced URL Filtering and Advanced DNS Security identify known domains and URLs associated with this activity as malicious. Cortex XDR and XSIAM help to prevent the threats described in this article, by employing the Malware Prevention Engine . This approach combines several layers of protection, including Advanced WildFire , Behavioral Threat Protection and the Local Analysis module, to prevent both known and unknown malware from causing harm to endpoints. If you think you may have been compromised or have an urgent matter, get in touch with the Unit 42 Incident Response team or call: North America Toll-Free: 866.486.4842 (866.4.UNIT42) EMEA: +31.20.299.3130 APAC: +65.6983.8730 Japan: +81.50.1790.0200 Palo Alto Networks has shared these findings with our fellow Cyber Threat Alliance (CTA) members. CTA members use this intelligence to rapidly deploy protections to their customers and to systematically disrupt malicious cyber actors. Learn more about the Cyber Threat Alliance . Indicators of Compromise Malicious destination IP addresses 2.26.98[.]67 62.60.179[.]230 87.120.107[.]33 91.92.243[.]29 103.245.236[.]146 178.16.54[.]31 178.16.54[.]109 194.76.227[.]94 206.189.229[.]43 Malware samples 01a96eeafb72042b3f69afd21b4c9155dbfe7f97ab3dca392972ad531a075ac2 9639f7ebc6a6d69d7bf5b8bc869e7783a1406088f192868624ad8919e9bfd1d4 bf24277400cc453d530e4277d3bd24e96c5e409adef6970518bdc59205aa0241 e310476c41ae4f6e3c4ed9bb88303ee6e5e1455bd7afe51cf48965ea7599e6e5 e3513922666c202c1ae5c06eea277ba10477868d6d89ce2819f4f8ff9070bc85 e5715e6611ef6bcb233f5d2098510dab3db408abbb728b00e1821bb255829373 A dditional Resources Phorpiex (Malware Family) – Malpedia Old Wine in the New Bottle: Mirai Variant Targets Multiple IoT Devices – Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 It Was Not Me! Malware-Initiated Vulnerability Scanning Is on the Rise – Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 Appendix: What Is ZT-IP? ZT-IP, which we have also called No-DNS or D2IP detection , extends the zero trust security model to IP-based traffic. This ensures that network services only connect to IP addresses previously resolved and approved by a trusted DNS service. Outbound connections to an IP address without a prior, valid DNS query are flagged as suspicious and blocked. In Figure 9, ZT-IP secures the network and firewall level through a simple enforcement mechanism: Figure 9. The security model of ZT-IP. The mechanism: Tracking legitimate IP addresses: The system monitors all valid DNS responses to learn which IP addresses are approved for outbound connections Building a trust list: These approved IP addresses are tracked in a secure list, along with a time limit for how long they remain valid Enforcement: Whenever a device attempts an outbound connection to an IP address, the firewall checks this list Blocking bypass attempts: The connection is only allowed if the destination IP address was recently approved by DNS. If an IP address is not on the list or its approved time limit has expired, the connection is immediately flagged as a potentialNo-DNS threat and blocked. Because some legitimate network protocols (such as DNS, Neighbor Discovery Protocol, VoIP, P2P and certain IoT services) connect directly to IP addresses by design, ZT-IP incorporates mechanisms to prevent false positives. It uses allowlists that exempt private intranet IP addresses, specific trusted network protocols and well-known benign public IP addresses from these strict DNS checks. ZT-IP delivers the following key advantages for network defense: Stops patient zero attacks: It proactively blocks unknown C2 callbacks and malware attempting to phone home using hard-coded IP addresses Secures shared infrastructure: It differentiates between legitimate traffic and malicious connections targeting the same shared cloud hosting environments, securely blocking the malicious traffic because it lacks the necessary DNS context Network-level protection: By operating at the firewall level, ZT-IP secures environments like IoT and operational technology (OT) without requiring endpoint agents to be installed on every single device

body_text: Optimum Reports Second Quarter 2026 Results August 06, 2026 7:00am EDT Download as PDF Related Documents Earnings Webcast Audio Presentation PDF Trended Schedule PDF NEW YORK--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Optimum Communications, Inc. (NYSE: OPTU) today reports results for the second quarter ended June 30, 2026. Dennis Mathew, Optimum Chairman and Chief Executive Officer , said: "Our second quarter results reflect disciplined execution across every part of our business. We expanded gross margin and Adjusted EBITDA margin, drove sequential improvement in broadband trends, delivered our best second-quarter mobile line growth to date, grew convergence ARPU year over year, and continued to expand our footprint, all while reducing operating expenses and simplifying how we operate. We are sharpening our go-to-market approach, deepening customer relationships through convergence, and transforming the customer experience to support stronger broadband performance over time. At the same time, we continue to take deliberate steps to strengthen our financial foundation, which remains a top priority as we position the business for long-term success. We remain focused on executing every day, investing where we see the strongest returns, and delivering best-in-class connectivity to the communities we serve." Second Quarter 2026 Overview Total revenue of $2.02 billion in Q2 2026 (-5.8% year over year) Residential revenue of $1.54 billion in Q2 2026 (-6.7% year over year) Residential average revenue per user (ARPU)(1) of $132.22 (-1.1% year over year) Convergence ARPU(2) of $79.80 (+2.4% year over year) Net loss attributable to stockholders of ($291.8) million (($0.67)/share on a diluted basis) in Q2 2026 , compared to ($96.3) million (($0.21)/share on a diluted basis) in Q2 2025. Net Losses of 40k Total broadband primary service units (PSUs) net losses of -40k in Q2 2026, which benefited from a bulk agreement, compared to -35k in Q2 2025, ending total broadband subscribers of 4.0 million Sharpening go-to-market execution through simpler offers and pricing and packaging enhancements, supporting gross add performance Enhancing customer retention through data-driven base management and proactive customer engagement Continued higher-speed tier adoption, with 53% of the residential broadband customer base taking 1 Gig or higher speeds at the end of Q2 2026, up from 38% in Q2 2025 Growing Through Mobile; Private Placement of Preferred Units On May 29, 2026, CSC Investments II LLC (“CSC II”), an indirect wholly owned subsidiary of Optimum Communications, Inc. completed a private placement of newly issued Series A Preferred Units to certain institutional accredited investors for an aggregate purchase price of $300 million. The proceeds from the private placement were used for general corporate purposes, including financing a tender offer and paying related transaction expenses. The Preferred Units are perpetual preferred interests in CSC II, with quarterly dividends payable in cash or by compounding, at CSC II’s option. Dividends accrue at 13.0% per year if paid in cash or 15.0% per year if compounded, and the rate may increase by 2.0% per year during certain triggering events. The Preferred Units may be redeemed by CSC II at any time, subject to the applicable redemption price, and are subject to mandatory redemption upon certain events involving CSC II and its subsidiaries. Private Exchange Transaction In a private exchange transaction completed on May 29, 2026, CSC II issued additional Preferred Units with an aggregate initial stated value of $212.5 million to Next Partner, L.P. and certain members of Optimum’s board of directors and executive management in exchange for shares of Optimum Class A and Class B common stock. Such exchanged common shares were not canceled. Cash Tender Offer In July 2026, CSC II completed its tender offer to purchase shares of Class A common stock of Optimum Communications, Inc. from unaffiliated stockholders at a purchase price of $2.50 per share. In accordance with the terms and conditions of the tender offer, CSC II accepted for purchase 120 million shares for an aggregate purchase price of $300 million, excluding fees and expenses related to the tender offer. Such purchased common shares were not canceled. define Adjusted EBITDA, which is a non-GAAP financial measure, as net income (loss) excluding income taxes, non-operating income or expenses, gain (loss) on extinguishment of debt and write-off of We define Adjusted EBITDA margin as Adjusted EBITDA divided by total revenue. Adjusted EBITDA eliminates the significant non-cash depreciation and amortization expense that results from the capital-intensive nature of our business and from intangible assets recognized from acquisitions, as well as certain non-cash and other operating items that affect the period-to-period comparability of our operating performance. In addition, Adjusted EBITDA is unaffected by our capital and tax structures and by our investment activities. We believe Adjusted EBITDA is an appropriate measure for evaluating our operating performance. Adjusted EBITDA and similar measures with similar titles are common performance measures used by investors, analysts and peers to compare performance in our industry. Internally, we use revenue and Adjusted EBITDA measures as important indicators of our business performance and evaluate management’s effectiveness with specific reference to these indicators. We believe Adjusted EBITDA provides management and investors a useful measure for period-to-period comparisons of our core business and operating results by excluding items that are not comparable across reporting periods or that do not otherwise relate to our ongoing operating results. Adjusted EBITDA should be viewed as a supplement to and not a substitute for operating income (loss), net income (loss), and other measures of performance presented in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles (“GAAP”). Since Adjusted EBITDA is not a measure of performance calculated in accordance with GAAP, this measure may not be comparable to similar measures with similar titles used by other companies. We also use Free Cash Flow (defined as net cash flows from operating activities less cash capital expenditures) as a liquidity measure. We believe this measure is useful to investors in evaluating our ability to service our debt and make continuing investments with internally generated funds, although it may not be directly comparable to similar measures reported by other companies. title: Explore the global benefits of preventive self-care, including improved health outcomes, healthcare savings and stronger health systems.
summary: Discover how preventive self-care can improve health outcomes, strengthen health systems and empower people to take greater control of their everyday health.
body_text: Ed Petter, Haleon’s Chief Corporate Affairs Officer and Chair of the Global Self-Care Federation, explains why preventive self-care is one of the fastest and most scalable ways to improve health outcomes, strengthen health systems and deliver economic value. Haleon’s science-backed brands, including Sensodyne, Voltaren, Otrivin and Centrum, support everyday self-care through better oral health, pain relief, respiratory health and nutritional wellbeing. By improving health literacy, expanding access to trusted self-care products and supporting healthcare professionals, Haleon is helping millions more people take greater control of their health. The value of preventive self-care is clear, but I believe one fundamental challenge remains: too many people still lack confidence in managing their own health. In Europe, 8 in 10 people say they feel responsible for managing their health, yet only 2 in 10 feel confident doing so. Closing this gap is critical, which is why initiatives that build awareness and understanding of self-care matter. While International Self-Care Month and International Self-Care Day in July help focus attention on this challenge, building people’s confidence to practise self-care should be a year-round priority. Self-care is not just about treating minor symptoms. It is about simple, consistent actions that help people prevent more serious illness, manage symptoms earlier and stay well - from brushing twice daily with fluoride toothpaste, which can reduce tooth decay by around 24%, to supporting digestive health, taking multivitamins to fill gaps in nutrition, and acting on pain early. At scale, the benefits are significant. The latest research from the Global Self-Care Federation shows that self-care practices generate around $144 billion in savings, including through avoidable physician visits and the cost of prescription medicines. Giving people the tools to manage their own health has also added 24 million high-quality years of life globally and saved more than 43.6 billion productive days – showing the social and economic value of self-care. Closing the gap between knowing and doing For me, this lack of confidence is one of the biggest missed opportunities in global health. People are surrounded by health information, but too often lack the trusted guidance, tools and support to know what is safe, effective and right for them. To unlock the full value of preventive self-care, policy and industry action must help people turn intention into action: Building health literacy: People need clear, practical and culturally relevant information they can act on - whether recognising symptoms earlier, understanding treatment options or building healthier everyday habits. Expanding access: Self-care is only possible when everyday health products, services and information are available, affordable and accessible - particularly in underserved communities. Supporting healthcare professionals: Pharmacists, dentists and other frontline professionals play a critical role in translating health information into trusted advice and helping people act with confidence. Haleon’s role in advancing preventive self-care As a consumer company focused solely on better everyday health, Haleon has a clear role in making self-care easier to understand, access and practise. Our trusted, science-backed brands – such as Sensodyne, Voltaren, Otrivin and Centrum - are used by more than one billion people worldwide, and we aim to reach a billion more by 2030. They help make prevention part of daily life: building oral health habits, helping people manage pain earlier, supporting respiratory health and bringing vitamins within reach for more consumers. Haleon is focusing our efforts on the barriers where we can make the greatest difference: Building health literacy and condition awareness: The Haleon Health Partner Portal provides free tools and resources for healthcare professionals to better support patients. In 2025, its expanded content and reach empowered more than 52m people globally through health professional engagement. In addition, in India, Sensodyne’s Chill Test uses a simple cold drink test to help people recognise tooth sensitivity earlier and act before issues worsen. Expanding access: Smaller, more affordable formats help bring everyday health within reach - from our 20-rupee Sensodyne pack in India, designed to support around 200 million lower-income consumers with tooth sensitivity, to Centrum single sachets in Brazil that address local needs around energy and immunity. Tackling bias and exclusion: Through tools such as our Health Inclusivity Screener, we are working to make health information and marketing more accessible, inclusive and representative. A shared opportunity to redefine prevention Preventive self-care can improve health outcomes at scale, but its potential depends on giving people the knowledge, access and confidence to act. The opportunity now is to make self-care a more integral part of health. That requires collective effort from policymakers, healthcare professionals, NGOs and industry to improve health literacy, expand access to trusted health solutions and empower people to take a more active role in managing their health. As health systems face growing pressure, prevention must play a bigger role in improving outcomes and building resilience. Self-care is not a substitute for professional healthcare, but it can help people manage everyday health and make more informed decisions about when and how to seek care. By making self-care simpler, more accessible and more inclusive, we can empower more people to take greater control of their health. The result is healthier populations, more sustainable health systems and better outcomes for society. Now is the time for health leaders, policymakers and industry to recognise self-care as a core pillar of prevention - and act together to make it part of how health is understood, supported and delivered.

title: Arbutus Reports Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Provides Corporate Update
summary: The Investor Relations website contains information about Arbutus Biopharma Corporation's business for stockholders, potential investors, and financial analysts.
body_text: Maintained strong financial position with cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities of $92.6M as of June 30, 2026 Received first payment of approximately $178M from Moderna settlement in July and expects to return up to approximately $230M in capital to Arbutus shareholders Filed three international patent enforcement lawsuits against Pfizer and BioNTech related to lipid nanoparticle (LNP) technology Achieved alignment with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) on a proposed imdusiran Phase 2b clinical trial design WARMINSTER, Pa., Aug. 12, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Arbutus Biopharma Corporation (Nasdaq: ABUS) (“Arbutus” or the “Company”), a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on infectious disease, today reported second quarter 2026 financial results and provided a corporate update. LNP Litigation On March 3, 2026, Arbutus, along with its exclusive licensee, Genevant Sciences (“Genevant”), entered into a settlement agreement to resolve all global patent infringement litigation and patent revocation proceedings involving Moderna. As part of the settlement, Moderna paid Arbutus and Genevant $950 million in July 2026 (the “Noncontingent Settlement Payment”) and will pay an additional $1.3 billion contingent upon an appellate ruling that 28 U.S.C. §1498 does not bar Arbutus’ and Genevant’s claims against Moderna for patent infringement, except as to doses characterized by the district court as having gone to U.S. government employees. On July 8, 2026, the Company received $178.4 million as its share of the Noncontingent Settlement Payment, which includes reimbursement of the Company’s litigation costs. In addition, the Company owns approximately 16% of the outstanding common equity of Genevant and anticipates the payment of a material dividend from Genevant in the third quarter of 2026. For more information about the terms and conditions of the settlement with Moderna, including the contingent payment, please refer to Arbutus’ Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q to be filed with the SEC on August 12, 2026 and Annual Report on Form 10-K filed with the SEC on March 23, 2026. In July 2026, the Company, along with Genevant, filed three international lawsuits against Pfizer, BioNTech and certain of their affiliates seeking to enforce patents protecting the Company’s patented LNP technology across 21 countries. Corporate Updates Arbutus expects to return capital to shareholders commencing in Q3 2026 through repurchases of up to approximately $230 million of the Company’s common shares, which repurchases may come in the form of a tender offer (including a modified “Dutch Auction” tender offer), open market purchases, accelerated share repurchases or other means. The specific form(s) of any such transaction(s) remains subject to the approval of the Company’s board of directors, and no assurance can be given that any such repurchase activity will occur in Q3 2026, or at all. In April 2026, the FDA granted Fast Track designation for imdusiran for the treatment of chronic hepatitis B (“cHBV”). The FDA’s Fast Track program is designed to facilitate the development and expedite the review of investigational therapies to treat serious conditions with unmet medical need. In May 2026, the Company reached alignment with the FDA on the design and safety parameters of a proposed Phase 2b clinical trial evaluating imdusiran for the treatment of cHBV. The Company intends to incorporate the FDA’s feedback into a final Phase 2b protocol. “This has been an exciting quarter for our imdusiran development program,” said Lindsay Androski, President and CEO of Arbutus. “In addition to obtaining Fast Track designation from the FDA on this promising drug candidate, which has achieved functional cure in 10 chronic hepatitis B patients to date, we reached alignment with the FDA on the design of our Phase 2b clinical trial. I would like to publicly congratulate our research and development team for their hard work and dedication in achieving these important milestones.” Financial Results Cash, Cash Equivalents and Investments As of June 30, 2026, the Company had cash, cash equivalents and investments in marketable securities of $92.6 million compared to $91.5 million as of December 31, 2025. During the six months ended June 30, 2026, the Company used $14.1 million in operating activities, which included one-time payments related to its restructuring efforts, and received $14.7 million of proceeds from the exercise of stock options. Revenue Total revenue was $1.0 million for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, compared to $10.7 million for the same period in 2025. The decrease of $9.7 million was due primarily to recognizing in the quarter ended June 30, 2025 all $9.6 million of previously deferred revenue upon conclusion of the Company’s strategic partnership with Qilu in June 2025. Operating Expenses Research and development expenses were $2.9 million for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, compared to $5.5 million for the same period in 2025. The decrease of $2.6 million was due primarily to cost savings from the Company’s decisions to reduce its workforce and discontinue in-house scientific research, as well as lower clinical trial costs as studies neared completion. General and administrative expenses were $3.9 million for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, compared to $3.3 million for the same period in 2025. This increase was due primarily to higher stock compensation expenses. There were no restructuring costs in the quarter ended June 30, 2026, compared to $0.2 million for the same period in 2025. Net Income/Loss For the quarter ended June 30, 2026, the Company’s net loss was $5.1 million, or a loss of $0.03 per basic and diluted common share, as compared to net income of $2.5 million, or income of $0.01 per basic and diluted common share, for the quarter ended June 30, 2025. Outstanding Shares As of June 30, 2026, the Company had 197.6 million common shares issued and outstanding, as well as 8.6 million stock options and unvested restricted stock units outstanding. 92,625 $ 98,088 About Imdusiran (AB-729) Imdusiran is an RNAi therapeutic specifically designed to reduce all hepatitis B viral proteins and antigens, including hepatitis B surface antigen (“HBsAg”), which is thought to be a key prerequisite to enable reawakening of a patient’s immune system to control the virus. Imdusiran targets hepatocytes using Arbutus’ novel covalently conjugated N -Acetylgalactosamine delivery technology enabling subcutaneous delivery. In Arbutus’ Phase 2a clinical trials, eight patients with cHBV achieved functional cure following treatment with imdusiran and nucleos(t)ide analogue (“NA”) therapy in combination with either pegylated interferon alfa-2a or low dose nivolumab plus an immunotherapeutic, with six out of the eight patients continuing to sustain functional cure for over two years. An additional 41 patients across the Company’s Phase 2a clinical trials were able to remain off NA therapy for at least 48 weeks during their Phase 2a clinical trials following treatment with imdusiran. Two additional patients who discontinued NA therapy in their Phase 2a clinical trials have now achieved functional cure during their participation in long-term follow-up. Functional cure is defined as sustained HBsAg seroclearance and hepatitis B virus deoxyribonucleic acid (“HBV DNA”) less than the lower limit of quantification after 24 weeks off treatment, with or without anti-hepatitis B surface antibodies. Clinical data generated thus far has shown imdusiran to be generally safe and well-tolerated, while also providing meaningful reductions in HBsAg and HBV DNA. About HBV Hepatitis B is a potentially life-threatening liver infection caused by hepatitis B virus (“HBV”). HBV can cause chronic infection which leads to a higher risk of death from cirrhosis and liver cancer. cHBV infection represents a significant unmet medical need. The World Health Organization estimates that over 250 million people worldwide suffer from cHBV infection, while other estimates indicate that approximately 2 million people in the United States suffer from cHBV infection. Approximately 1.1 million people die every year from complications related to cHBV infection despite the availability of effective vaccines and current treatment options. About Arbutus Arbutus Biopharma Corporation (Nasdaq: ABUS) is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on infectious disease. The Company is currently developing imdusiran (AB-729) and an oral PD-L1 inhibitor (AB-101) for the treatment of cHBV infection. The Company is also consulting closely with and supporting its exclusive licensee, Genevant, to protect and defend its intellectual property, which is the subject of on-going lawsuits against Pfizer/BioNTech for use of Arbutus’ patented LNP technology in their COVID-19 vaccines. For more information, visit www.arbutusbio.com . title: Wedding Guest Dress Code Guide
summary: Wedding dress codes range from ultra-formal white tie (floor-length gowns and tailcoats) to relaxed casual (sundresses and khakis). The most common codes
body_text: Last Updated on August 12, 2026 by Joy Editors Wedding dress codes range from ultra-formal white tie (floor-length gowns and tailcoats) to relaxed casual (sundresses and khakis). The most common codes for 2026 weddings are black tie, black tie optional, cocktail, semi-formal, dressy casual, and casual. When in doubt, check the couple’s wedding website for specifics, or use venue type, time of day, and season as your guide. It is always safer to be slightly overdressed than underdressed. You received the invitation, marked your calendar, and then stopped cold at two words: “cocktail attire.” Or maybe “black tie optional.” Or, worse, the invitation said nothing at all about what to wear. You are not alone. Dress code confusion is one of the most common sources of pre-wedding stress for guests, and the terminology has only gotten more varied as couples customize their celebrations. This guide breaks down every wedding dress code you are likely to encounter in 2026, with specific outfit guidance for women, men, and anyone who prefers gender-neutral options. Quick-Reference: Wedding Dress Codes at a Glance Before diving into the details, here is a comparison table showing the full spectrum from most formal to most relaxed. Bookmark this for the next time an invitation lands in your mailbox. Dress Code Women Men Formality Level White Tie Floor-length ball gown, elbow-length gloves Black tailcoat, white bow tie, white vest Ultra-Formal Black Tie Floor-length gown or elegant cocktail dress Black tuxedo, black bow tie Very Formal Black Tie Optional Floor-length or dressy cocktail dress Tuxedo or dark formal suit Formal Formal / Black Tie Invited Floor-length or midi dress in rich fabric Dark suit, dress shirt, tie Formal Cocktail Knee-length or midi cocktail dress, dressy jumpsuit Dark suit, dress shirt, tie optional Dressy Semi-Formal Midi or knee-length dress, dressy separates Suit or blazer with dress pants Polished Dressy Casual Sundress, skirt-and-blouse combo, jumpsuit Blazer or sport coat, chinos, no tie Relaxed Elegant Casual Sundress, maxi dress, nice separates Button-down shirt, chinos or khakis Relaxed Beach / Resort Flowy maxi dress, linen dress Linen pants, guayabera or linen shirt Relaxed Garden Party Floral midi dress, tea-length dress Light suit or blazer with chinos Polished Relaxed White Tie White tie is the most formal dress code in existence, and it is rare at modern weddings. If you see it on an invitation, expect a grand venue (think: ballroom, estate, or historic mansion) and a ceremony that calls for the highest level of elegance. What Women Should Wear A floor-length ball gown in a luxurious fabric such as silk, satin, or organza Opera-length (elbow or longer) gloves are traditional, though optional in 2026 Refined jewelry: think diamonds, pearls, or statement pieces A small clutch and heels What Men Should Wear A black tailcoat (not a standard tuxedo) White wing-collar dress shirt White bow tie and white vest Black patent leather shoes Pro tip: White tie events almost always take place in the evening. If the invitation says “white tie” for a daytime event, treat it as “formal” instead, as the tailcoat is traditionally an after-6 p.m. garment. Black Tie Black tie is the most common formal dress code for evening weddings. It signals a polished, upscale event where guests should look their best. Unlike white tie, there is some flexibility in what constitutes appropriate attire. What Women Should Wear A floor-length evening gown is the traditional choice An elegant cocktail dress (knee-length or midi) in a rich fabric also works Jumpsuits in luxe materials like crepe or satin are increasingly popular Heels, dressy flats, or embellished sandals A clutch and statement jewelry What Men Should Wear A black tuxedo with satin or grosgrain lapels A white dress shirt (ideally with French cuffs) A black bow tie (not a long tie) Black patent leather oxfords or polished dress shoes Optional: cummerbund or vest Common mistake: Wearing a regular dark suit to a black tie event. While a dark charcoal suit can pass at black tie optional weddings, a true black tie invitation calls for a tuxedo. If you do not own one, renting is a practical option that typically costs between $100 and $250. Black Tie Optional This is where confusion often starts. “Black tie optional” means the couple would love to see tuxedos and gowns, but they understand that not every guest owns formalwear. You have permission to dress down one notch from black tie. What Women Should Wear A floor-length gown, a dressy cocktail dress, or an elegant midi dress Rich fabrics: silk, velvet, chiffon, or crepe Heels or dressy flats What Men Should Wear A tuxedo (if you have one) or a dark formal suit in navy, charcoal, or black A dress shirt and tie (a bow tie works too) Polished leather dress shoes Pro tip: When choosing between a tuxedo and a dark suit for a black tie optional wedding, consider the venue and time. An evening event at a ballroom leans toward tuxedo. An afternoon event at a vineyard leans toward a dark suit. Formal Attire “Formal” sits just below black tie and is common for evening weddings at upscale venues. The distinction is subtle: formal attire does not require a tuxedo, though one would not be out of place. What Women Should Wear A floor-length or midi dress in a structured, polished fabric A dressy pantsuit or tailored jumpsuit Closed-toe or strappy heels What Men Should Wear A dark suit (navy, charcoal, or black) with a dress shirt and tie A pocket square adds a polished finishing touch Leather dress shoes, freshly shined Cocktail Attire Cocktail is the single most common wedding dress code in 2026. It strikes the balance between formal and relaxed, making it the go-to for evening ceremonies at restaurants, rooftop venues, museums, and urban event spaces. What Women Should Wear A knee-length or midi cocktail dress (the classic choice) A dressy jumpsuit or chic separates (tailored pants with a blouse or structured top) Heels, block heels, or elegant mules A clutch or small evening bag What Men Should Wear A dark suit or a well-fitted blazer with dress trousers A dress shirt (tie is optional but adds polish) Leather loafers or lace-up dress shoes Common mistake: Wearing a floor-length gown to a cocktail wedding. A full-length dress can read as overdressed at a cocktail event and may feel out of place among shorter hemlines. Save the gown for black tie. Semi-Formal Attire Semi-formal is often confused with cocktail, and the two overlap significantly. The key difference: semi-formal leans slightly more relaxed and is commonly used for afternoon or early evening weddings. For a deeper dive into exactly what this dress code means, check out our guide to semi-formal wedding attire . What Women Should Wear A midi or knee-length dress in a polished fabric Dressy separates (a skirt and blouse, or tailored pants with a top) Block heels, wedges, or dressy flats What Men Should Wear A suit (lighter colors are acceptable for daytime) or a blazer with dress pants A dress shirt with or without a tie Loafers or leather dress shoes Semi-Formal vs. Cocktail: A Side-by-Side Comparison Factor Semi-Formal Cocktail Typical time of day Afternoon or early evening Evening Women’s hemline Knee-length or midi Knee-length or midi (dressier fabrics) Men’s suit Suit or blazer combo Dark suit preferred Tie required? No Optional (adds polish) Overall vibe Polished but approachable Refined and evening-ready Dressy Casual (Smart Casual) Dressy casual (sometimes called smart casual) is a step down from semi-formal. The goal is to look put-together without being overly formal. Think of it as what you would wear to an upscale restaurant or a nice rooftop party. What Women Should Wear A sundress, wrap dress, or midi skirt with a polished top A jumpsuit in a solid color or subtle print Wedges, block heels, or stylish flats What Men Should Wear A blazer or sport coat with chinos or dress pants (no jeans) A button-down shirt, open collar, no tie needed Loafers, clean leather shoes, or suede bucks Casual A casual wedding dress code does not mean jeans and sneakers. “Casual” in the wedding context still means polished and intentional. Think of it as your best version of everyday clothes. What Women Should Wear A sundress, cotton maxi dress, or a skirt-and-top combination Sandals, wedges, or clean flats Light, simple jewelry What Men Should Wear A button-down or polo shirt with chinos or dress shorts (venue dependent) Loafers, clean sneakers, or boat shoes Skip the tie and blazer unless you want the extra polish Pro tip: Even at a casual wedding, avoid distressed denim, flip-flops, athletic wear, and graphic tees. The couple chose “casual” to make you comfortable, not to suggest you skip getting dressed up entirely. Beach and Resort Beach and resort weddings have their own unwritten rules. The dress code needs to account for sand, sun, wind, and potentially warm temperatures, while still honoring the significance of the occasion. What Women Should Wear A flowy maxi dress or airy midi dress in lightweight fabric (chiffon, cotton, linen) Bright colors and tropical prints are welcome Wedges, block heels, or dressy flat sandals (stilettos sink in sand) Skip heavy jewelry. Keep accessories simple and weather-appropriate. What Men Should Wear Linen pants or cotton chinos with a linen shirt or guayabera Light colors: tan, cream, light blue, soft pastels Leather sandals or loafers (no socks with sandals) A sport coat is optional and often unnecessary in tropical heat Common mistake: Wearing all white to a beach wedding. White linen might feel thematically right for the setting, but it is still reserved for the couple. Choose cream, light blue, sage, or coral instead. Garden Party Garden party attire calls for polished, outdoor-appropriate outfits with a hint of whimsy. Florals, pastels, and lightweight fabrics are your friends. The formality level sits between semi-formal and dressy casual. What Women Should Wear A floral midi dress, tea-length dress, or printed jumpsuit Light fabrics: cotton, chiffon, or eyelet Wedges or block heels (the lawn will thank you) A wide-brimmed hat or fascinator adds a festive touch What Men Should Wear A light-colored suit (tan, light grey, blue) or a blazer with chinos A patterned or pastel dress shirt, with or without a tie Loafers or suede shoes Rustic, Western, and Country Rustic or country weddings often take place at barns, ranches, farms, or outdoor venues. The dress code is relaxed but still intentional. Western-themed weddings may lean into specific aesthetic choices. What Women Should Wear A midi dress, maxi dress, or floral print dress Cowboy boots (if the theme calls for it) or ankle boots A denim jacket as a layer for cooler evenings What Men Should Wear Dark jeans or chinos with a button-down or Western shirt Cowboy boots, clean work boots, or leather shoes A sport coat is a nice touch but not required A bolo tie or a hat, if the couple embraces the Western theme Festive Attire “Festive” is a newer dress code that signals the couple wants guests to have fun with their outfits. It is common for holiday weddings, themed celebrations, or couples who want a colorful, high-energy atmosphere. What It Means Bold colors, metallics, sequins, or statement prints are encouraged The formality level typically falls between cocktail and semi-formal The couple is asking you to dress up and express personality Pro tip: When an invitation says “festive,” check the wedding website for color palette hints or theme details. Many couples provide additional guidance on their online wedding website to help guests nail the look. Creative Black Tie Creative black tie gives guests permission to put a personal spin on formal attire. The base is black tie, but you can add a unique twist through color, pattern, accessories, or silhouette. What Women Should Wear A floor-length gown in an unexpected color or bold print A dramatic jumpsuit or unconventional silhouette Statement accessories: oversized earrings, a colored clutch, or unexpected shoes What Men Should Wear A tuxedo with a twist: a velvet jacket, a colored bow tie, patterned cummerbund, or unique lapel pins A dinner jacket in a non-black color (midnight blue, burgundy, emerald) Dress shoes in an unexpected finish (suede, patent with color) What to Do When No Dress Code Is Listed Many invitations skip the dress code entirely. When that happens, do not panic. Use this three-step decision framework to determine the right formality level. Step 1: Consider the Venue Hotel ballroom, country club, or estate: Lean formal or cocktail Restaurant, rooftop, or gallery: Lean cocktail or semi-formal Barn, backyard, or public park: Lean dressy casual or casual Beach, resort, or destination: Lean beach/resort casual Step 2: Consider the Time of Day Morning or afternoon: Lighter colors, less formal fabrics Late afternoon to evening: Darker colors, more formal fabrics Nighttime: Cocktail or formal, depending on venue Step 3: Consider the Season Spring/Summer: Lighter fabrics, brighter colors, open-toe shoes acceptable Fall/Winter: Richer fabrics (velvet, wool, crepe), deeper colors, closed-toe shoes If you are still unsure after running through all three steps, reach for cocktail attire. It is the safest middle ground for most weddings. You can also check the couple’s wedding website, where many couples include dress code details even if the physical invitation does not mention them. 2026 Wedding Dress Code Trends Wedding fashion evolves each year, and 2026 has introduced a few notable shifts worth knowing about. Color-Coded Weddings More couples are asking guests to wear specific color palettes rather than traditional dress codes. You might see “earth tones only” or “jewel tones encouraged” on an invitation. This trend prioritizes aesthetic cohesion in photos and creates a striking visual effect. Quiet Luxury The “quiet luxury” aesthetic has moved from streetwear into wedding fashion. For guests, this means understated, high-quality pieces in neutral tones: well-tailored suits, simple silk dresses, minimal jewelry. The look is expensive without being flashy. Gender-Neutral and Non-Binary Fashion Wedding fashion is becoming more inclusive in 2026. If traditional “women’s” or “men’s” categories do not fit you, focus on the formality level rather than the specific garment type. A well-tailored suit, a structured jumpsuit, or a flowing ensemble all work beautifully when they match the event’s level of dress. Elevated Casual Casual weddings are getting more popular, but “casual” keeps getting redefined upward. The 2026 version of a casual wedding guest outfit involves thoughtful layering, intentional accessories, and natural fabrics rather than the “just throw something on” approach. Universal Rules Every Wedding Guest Should Know No matter the dress code, these rules apply to every wedding you attend. Never wear white, ivory, or champagne unless the couple explicitly requests it. This includes dresses with a white base and minimal print. Do not upstage the couple. Skip overly revealing outfits, all-red ensembles at some cultural ceremonies, and anything designed to attract maximum attention. When in doubt, overdress. Being slightly more formal than the dress code is always more comfortable than being underdressed. Nobody has ever regretted wearing a blazer. Wear comfortable shoes or bring a backup pair. Most wedding celebrations involve standing, walking, and dancing for hours. Check the wedding website. Couples often add dress code details, venue specifics, and even outfit inspiration to their wedding website pages . Jumpsuits and pantsuits are welcome at nearly every formality level in 2026. Match the fabric and structure to the dress code, and you will be appropriately dressed. For Couples: How to Choose and Communicate Your Dress Code If you are planning a wedding, choosing the right dress code and communicating it clearly can prevent confusion and help your guests feel confident about what to wear. How to Pick the Right Dress Code Match your dress code to three factors: Your venue. A black tie dress code at a barn wedding will confuse guests. A casual dress code at a grand ballroom will leave them underdressed. Let the venue guide the formality. Your guest list. If many of your guests are traveling or have limited budgets, consider how accessible the dress code is. Cocktail and semi-formal are the most universally achievable. Your own style. The dress code should match the overall aesthetic you are creating. If your celebration is relaxed and personal, a formal dress code may feel out of sync. How to Communicate the Dress Code Include the dress code on your invitation (typically in the lower-right corner for print invitations) and on your wedding website. Many guests will check online for details, so make your digital invitations a source of clarity. Here are wording templates you can use on your invitations or website: Black tie: “Black tie attire requested” Black tie optional: “Black tie optional. Formal attire is welcome.” Cocktail: “Cocktail attire, please” Semi-formal: “Semi-formal attire is encouraged” Dressy casual: “Dressy casual attire. Think polished and comfortable.” Beach: “Beach formal. Light, elegant attire is perfect for our oceanside celebration.” Color theme: “We would love to see our guests in shades of blue and green.” Pro tip: Add a short FAQ to your wedding website addressing dress code questions. A line like “What should I wear? Cocktail attire. Think a knee-length dress or a dark suit.” removes almost all guesswork. You can set this up on your wedding planning help center pages or directly on your event details page. Budget-Friendly Outfit Strategies Wedding season can get expensive, especially if you are attending multiple events. Here are practical ways to dress appropriately without overspending. Rent formal wear. Tuxedo and suit rentals typically cost $100 to $250, and women’s dress rental services offer designer pieces for a fraction of the retail price. Rewear and restyle. A solid-color dress or a well-fitted suit can serve across multiple dress codes with different accessories. Swap the shoes, add a scarf, or change the tie. Shop secondhand. Consignment stores and online resale platforms often carry barely-worn formalwear at significant discounts. Invest in one versatile piece. A dark suit for men or a well-cut midi dress for women can work from cocktail through semi-formal, making it the highest-ROI wedding wardrobe item. Seasonal Dress Code Adjustments The same dress code can look quite different depending on the season. Here is how to adapt your outfit for comfort and style. Summer Weddings Choose breathable fabrics: linen, cotton, lightweight wool, or chiffon Lighter suit colors (light grey, tan) are appropriate for semi-formal and below Open-toe shoes are fine for cocktail and below Skip heavy layers; a lightweight blazer is enough for air-conditioned venues Winter Weddings Rich fabrics work well: velvet, brocade, heavy crepe, wool blends Deeper colors (burgundy, emerald, navy, plum) feel seasonally appropriate Closed-toe shoes and boots (if the venue and dress code allow it) Bring a dress coat; parkas and puffer jackets should not be your arrival statement Frequently Asked Questions What are the most common wedding dress codes? The most common wedding dress codes in 2026 are cocktail, semi-formal, black tie optional, and dressy casual. Cocktail is the single most popular choice for evening weddings at urban venues, while semi-formal covers most afternoon celebrations. Beach and garden party codes are common for outdoor and destination weddings. What is the difference between black tie and black tie optional? Black tie means guests should wear a tuxedo (men) or floor-length gown (women). Black tie optional means a tuxedo or gown is ideal, but a dark formal suit or dressy cocktail dress is also appropriate. The “optional” gives guests flexibility to dress one notch below full black tie. What should I wear if the wedding invitation does not list a dress code? Use the venue, time of day, and season to guide your choice. A hotel ballroom in the evening suggests cocktail or formal attire. A backyard afternoon celebration suggests dressy casual. When you cannot determine the formality, cocktail attire is the safest default. Check the couple’s wedding website for additional details. Is cocktail attire the same as semi-formal? They are similar but not identical. Cocktail attire is slightly more formal and typically associated with evening events. Semi-formal is more flexible, works for afternoon or early evening, and allows lighter colors and fabrics. For cocktail, think dark suits and knee-length dresses in polished fabrics. For semi-formal, a blazer with dress pants or a midi dress in a lighter fabric works well. Can I wear a jumpsuit or pantsuit to a wedding? Yes. Jumpsuits and pantsuits are welcome at nearly every wedding dress code level in 2026. The key is matching the fabric and structure to the formality. A tailored crepe jumpsuit works for black tie optional. A relaxed linen jumpsuit suits a beach or casual wedding. Focus on fit and fabric rather than the garment category. Can I wear black to a wedding? Yes, wearing black to a wedding is widely accepted in 2026. A black cocktail dress, black suit, or black jumpsuit is appropriate for most dress codes. The only time to reconsider is if the couple specifies a colorful theme or if the wedding has cultural traditions where black carries negative connotations. When in doubt, check the wedding website or ask the couple.

title: Review: Singapore Airlines First Class Suites on the Airbus A380
summary: Singapore Airlines operates what is arguably the most spacious and luxurious first class product in the sky today.
body_text: Review: Singapore Airlines First Class Suites on the Airbus A380 By Tim Qin - Updated: August 6, 2026 Singapore Airlines operates what is arguably the most spacious and luxurious first class product in the sky today. I recently flew the iconic Singapore Airlines First Class Suites on the Airbus A380 for the first time, traveling nonstop from Singapore to Delhi. From the private check-in terminal at Changi to the double bed at 35,000 feet, every detail was meticulously executed. How to book Singapore Airlines First Class Suites Finding First Class Suites availability can be notoriously difficult, but I managed to lock in two connected suites on the exact same flight using credit card points. To find the award availability without manually searching, I set up custom flight alerts using the Roame award flight search tool and booked the moment I received the text alert. (Unfortunately, Singapore Airlines now makes it almost impossible to search award flights now.) I transferred American Express points directly to the Singapore Airlines KrisFlyer loyalty program. For this short-haul route from Singapore to Delhi, award redemptions start at 49,500 miles for saver fares, though it's much easier to find advantage fares for 98,000 miles. Pro Tip : While Singapore Airlines does not release Suites nor First Class award space to partner programs, you can regularly find availability directly through the KrisFlyer program. To figure out which credit card points transfer into Singapore Airlines before you book, consult the transfer partner cheat sheet . Live SkyView Up-to-date results with Live Search. Search up to 25 airline loyalty programs up to 365 days in any fare class within 10-15 seconds See deals instantly with SkyView. SkyView constantly checks flights for the top 6,500 routes so you can see your results instantly. Try Live Search Join Now Try SkyView Join Now Live SkyView If you're looking to book this exact seat with your own credit card points, check out the Roame guide on how to book Singapore Airlines First Class Suites with points to see which routes fly the A380 Suites. Airline Singapore Airlines Aircraft Airbus A380-800 Flight # SQ 406 Route Singapore Changi Airport (SIN) to Indira Gandhi International Airport (DEL) Duration 5 hours, 45 minutes Cabin & Layout 6 Suites in a 1-1 configuration Class First Class Suites Seat Suites 1A and 2A (connected double suite) Private First Class Check-in at Singapore Changi Airport Singapore Airlines provides a dedicated First Class Check-in Reception building at Changi Terminal 3 specifically for First Class and Solitaire PPS Club passengers. It is a completely separate driveway entrance where curbside staff greet you the moment your car stops, taking your luggage directly off your hands. It was giving high-end "White Lotus" luxury resort vibes. Instead of standing at a traditional counter, you are ushered into a private lounge where you rest on plush couches while agents process your passports and hand-deliver your boarding passes. From there, you led by a Singapore Airlines agent to a private immigration channel with zero wait time. Singapore Airlines Suites Class Lounge - The Private Room Before the flight, I hung out at The Private Room, which is only open to First and Suites Class passengers on Singapore Airlines operated flights. Note: Star Alliance partner First Class passengers do not have access and have to use the Krisflyer First Class Lounge next door. The Private Room feels like a private sanctuary in a busy airport. It’s an extremely quiet ~10,000 square feet lounge that fits a maximum of 78 guests. There was only two other travelers there and it was the middle of the day. The main seating area has a large area with lots of couches. Along the walls there are segmented “rooms” for privacy. There are also 4 private sleeping rooms that can be reserved for 2 hours at a time and 3 shower suites. For dining, they have an extensive à la carte menu where you can order anything you want. We tried for Lobster Bisque, dim sum platter, and assorted satay. Quite tasty! For drinks I tried the 2013 Taittinger Comtes de Champagne and the 2007 Charles Heidsieck blanc des millénaires (both bottles retails for ~$200). Cabin & Seats When it was time to board, we walked straight through the Suites Class only line directly onto the upper deck of the massive A380. We were greeted by name by nearly every crew member lining the entryway. The cabin features just six suites in a spacious 1-1 layout. Rather than converting your armchair into a flat bed, you get a dedicated 270-degree swiveling leather armchair upholstered by Poltrona Frau, alongside a completely separate, stowaway bed. While the separate swivel chair is nice in concept, it does not recline and you are swiveled to face the entrance of the suite during dinner service. It can feel quite awkward. We chose Suites 1A and 2A because they could be connected into 1 suite. Row 1 suites are extra-large, offering approximately 54 square feet of personal floor space. This makes them among the largest individual suites in commercial aviation. Each suite features 5-foot-high privacy walls, a smooth sliding door, and a full personal wardrobe closet that easily accommodates carry-on luggage and garments. If you are traveling with a companion, the middle partition between 1A/2A (or 1F/2F) can be lowered to form a massive double suite space. Photo courtesy of Singapore Airlines The 6 First Class Suites in a 1-1 configuration. There are also 78 Business Class seats in the upper cabin. Entertainment & Amenities In Suite 1A, you are treated to two separate screens: a wall-mounted display and a main 32-inch HD touchscreen monitor mounted on a motorized swivel arm. All room controls, including the 10-zone ambient lighting, window shades, and flight attendant calls, are managed via a detachable 7-inch tablet docking in the armrest. Singapore Airlines also provides top-of-the-line Bang & Olufsen noise-canceling headphones. Amenity-wise, we were presented with a signature Lalique amenity kit alongside Lalique-branded pajamas and slippers. The kit included full-size skincare items and a bottle of Lalique Encre Indigo cologne (though the scent was not for me). Unlimited complimentary Wi-Fi is provided for First Class passengers, though speeds during our flight were occasionally spotty. Dining - Food & Drinks The onboard culinary service was nothing short of spectacular. Upon settling into the suite, the crew immediately poured a welcome glass of 2015 Louis Roederer Cristal Champagne (retailing around $350 per bottle). For dinner we were served the 2005 Chateau Leoville Poyferre (also retailing around $375 per bottle). Singapore Airlines is famous for its "Book the Cook" service, which allows First Class passengers to pre-order from a menu of over 60 gourmet dishes up to 24 hours prior to departure. Overwhelmed by the options, I defaulted to the classic Lobster Thermidor, which was rich and perfectly cooked. The main meal service also featured an appetizer course of premium Kaluga Queen caviar accompanied by traditional garnishes, concluding with a light strawberry shortcake for dessert. Bathroom & Toiletries While Singapore Airlines opted not to install onboard showers like Emirates or Etihad, they made up for it through sheer spatial luxury. There are two massive lavatories dedicated exclusively to the six First Class passengers. The primary bathroom on the starboard side features a full sit-down vanity desk with a plush leather stool, a full-length mirror, and dedicated ring-lit vanity mirrors. The interior finishes utilize a high-end palette of grey faux marble, dark walnut wood paneling, and soft beige walls, with even the toilet discreetly disguised beneath a padded leather bench seat. Sleeping Experience Unlike almost every first-class product where the seat converts into a bed, Singapore Airlines provides a completely separate, stowaway 76-inch flatbed. You can easily transition between the chair and bed at will. When we were ready for bed, the crew transformed our individual rooms into a massive 97-square-foot (9 square meters) double suite. You can then combine the single beds into 1 shared double bed. The single bed is 27 inches wide and the double bed is 54 inches wide. It felt like a real bed. The bed is dressed in ultra-premium Lalique-embroidered linens, featuring a plush mattress topper, dual pillows, and a heavy cotton duvet. Because the bed is a dedicated surface, it feels way more stable and supportive than a reconfigured chair. Even when lights were off for sleeping, there was an attendant in a seat in the aisle offering to help. Unfortunately, the only thing missing was the Singapore Airlines teddy bear. It was not offered and I also forgot to ask. Final Thoughts: (10/10) I would 100% go out of my way fly again if I can find more points availability. Ratings Food Quality: 10/10 Drinks Quality: 10/10 Cleanliness: 10/10 Cabin Design: 10/10 Seat: 8/10 Service: 10/10
