body_text: A silk saree already does most of the work, the sheen, the weight, the drape. The blouse just has to keep up. Get the blouse model wrong and even the richest Banarasi or Kanjivaram can look unfinished. Get it right and the whole outfit feels deliberate, expensive, put-together. Here's how to think about picking a blouse model for a silk saree, whether you're dressing for a wedding, a puja, or just a Saturday that calls for something more than cotton. Pictured: Zohra x Luxe | Black Blouse with Gold Hand Embroidery and FlexiFit™ Elastic Sides Start with the saree's weight, not just its colour Heavier silks, Kanjivaram, Banarasi, tussar with zari, carry a lot of visual weight on their own. A blouse in a busy print or heavy embellishment can compete with the saree instead of complementing it. As a rule: the heavier and more ornate the saree, the simpler the blouse can afford to be, and vice versa. Heavily worked silk saree , pair with a solid-colour or subtly detailed blouse in a contrasting or tonal shade. Lighter or plainer silk saree , this is where a statement blouse (deep neck, puff sleeves, sequins) can really shine. Necklines that flatter silk drapes A deep neck blouse is a classic choice for silk sarees at evening functions, it opens up the neckline for statement jewellery, which silk sarees are often paired with. For daytime silk (like a lighter Mysore silk for a puja), a sweetheart neckline is a softer, equally flattering option that doesn't feel too formal. Sleeves: match the occasion, not just the trend Puff sleeves have become the default 'statement' choice for silk sarees at weddings and sangeets, the volume adds drama that matches the occasion. For more everyday silk (a work event, a family lunch) a sleeveless or simple elbow-sleeve blouse keeps things elegant without overdoing it. Pictured: Nargis x Rozaana | Corset-Style Blouse with FlexiFit™ Elastic Back Our shortcut: FlexiFit™ blouses in every model If you're buying a blouse to go with a specific silk saree, fit matters as much as the design, a blouse that gapes or pulls will undercut even the best-matched neckline. Our FlexiFit™ blouses come with a stretchable smocked back that adjusts to a range of sizes, so you can shop by design first and skip the tailor. Explore our full vegan silk saree and blouse edit for pre-matched silk pairings, or browse blouse models by neckline and sleeve in our complete blouse fit and style guide .

title: What It Takes to Move More Than Manufacturing: Lessons in Global Collaboration
summary: Moving a manufacturing site across continents is not just an operations challenge. It is a people and culture challenge. As we transition CO₂ laser manufacturing from Mukilteo, Washington, to Stockport, UK, we are seeing what global collaboration really requires.
body_text: By Andrew Carson, Sr. Director Engineering Solutions When organizations talk about site moves, the focus often centers on efficiency, cost, and infrastructure. The real challenge and the opportunity come from how teams across the world work together to execute as one. As we transition CO₂ laser manufacturing from Mukilteo, Washington, to Stockport, United Kingdom, we are seeing what it truly takes to align global teams around a shared goal. This effort spans multiple regions, including the United States, the United Kingdom, Europe, and Asia. Each team brings strengths that are shaped by the local environment and technical expertise. Where Cultural Differences Show Up Cultural differences are not abstract. They show up in everyday decisions, communication, and execution. In some European teams, there is a stronger reliance on defined structure. Work tends to follow clearly assigned ownership and formal processes. If a task is not explicitly assigned, it may not move forward right away. In the United States, teams are often more action-oriented. There is an expectation to take initiative and move forward when the path is clear, even without direct instruction. Communication styles also vary. Some teams communicate in a very direct and concise way. Feedback is delivered quickly and without much context. Other teams take more time to build alignment and provide background before making a point. Even within the United States, regional differences are noticeable. Teams in the Boston area often operate with a faster pace and more direct communication style, while teams in the Pacific Northwest tend to be more measured and collaborative in how they engage. These differences can create friction if they are not understood. A direct comment may be interpreted as abrupt. A pause for clarity may be seen as hesitation. In reality, these are simply different ways of working. Turning Differences into Better Execution Global collaboration does not mean forcing one way of working across all teams. It requires creating a shared understanding. One of the most effective approaches is moving beyond large, high-level meetings and focusing on smaller, cross-site working sessions. When individuals responsible for similar work connect directly, they can align on expectations and clarify differences to build trust more quickly. It is also important to identify individuals who can operate effectively across cultures. These employees combine technical expertise with adaptability and awareness. They recognize differences without being slowed down by them, and they help translate across teams. Building Trust Across Teams Trust is essential for global execution, and it is built through consistent behavior. Clear and honest communication is critical. Teams need realistic expectations, especially when it comes to timelines and deliverables. When leaders are transparent about constraints and challenges, teams are better equipped to respond. Respect also plays a central role. Every function contributes to the final outcome, from engineering and production to operations and support. Recognizing that interdependence keeps teams aligned and engaged. Trust is reinforced when teams see that their input is heard and reflected in decisions. A Stronger Way to Operate This site move is part of a broader effort to strengthen our global manufacturing footprint and better serve customers. It also reflects how we operate as a global organization. When we understand how different teams think, communicate, and execute, we can align those strengths instead of working against them. That leads to better decisions and stronger execution, which allows us to build more resilient operations. Global collaboration requires effort and intention. When done well, it becomes a meaningful advantage for our teams and for customers. That is how we continue building One Novanta.

title: Ambient Clinical Documentation in 2026: End the Note-Taking Burden
summary: Learn how ambient AI documentation captures patient conversations, generates SOAP notes, and reduces physician charting time in 2026.
body_text: In 2026, ambient AI technology is changing clinical workflows by reducing administrative workload and improving providers’ satisfaction. Most healthcare providers choose medicine because they want to take care of patients, not to devote their time to documenting every patient’s notes. Yet recording and managing patient information has become a major responsibility for many clinicians. Often prolonging workdays, contributing to burnout, and takes valuable time away from patients. Because healthcare organizations find solutions to decrease administrative burden while maintaining a high standard of care, ambient clinical documentation is standing as a strong solution. By managing much of the documentation process automatically, it facilitates clinicians to focus on meaningful patient interactions rather than manual work. Driven by recent advances in Artificial intelligence, an ambient clinical documentation tool can capture conversations with patients, then turn them into structured clinical notes, and automatically add them to Electronic Health Records (EHRs). Despite spending time creating patient notes manually, physicians can stay entirely involved in the conversation with the patient, and AI takes care of much of the notes in the background. Curious if you have the right staff in the right roles? Wondering how you can keep your staff incentivized and focused on the patient experience? Check out our free e-book, Staffing in the New Economy. Why Physicians Spend Half Their Day on Documentation Documentation has become one of the most time-intensive parts of healthcare. Between recording patient notes, updating charts, handling coding requirements, and meeting regulatory requirements. Providers often spend nearly as much time documenting care as they do deliver it. Many physicians find themselves completing charts after clinic hours. As compliance requirements and electronic health records (EHR) workflows have grown increasingly complex, the physician’s documentation burden has gradually increased. This makes it hard to stay productive without working beyond the end of the day. The traditional documentation method frequently switches repeatedly between engaging patients and data entry. Although voice-to-text tools in electronic health records (EHRs) have minimized the need for typing, they still require physicians to manually record notes and then structure the information once it is done. As patient volume rises and staffing challenges continue, healthcare organizations are finding ways to decrease administrative workload while maintaining accurate medical records. This demand has driven faster technology adoption like AI medical scribes and automated documentation platforms. What Ambient Clinical Documentation Actually Means: Ambient clinical documentation is described as AI-powered technology that listens to patient conversations automatically and makes clinical notes. As opposed to a traditional dictation tool, the ambient system runs silently in the background without the need for a physician to manually speak out every detail. They use advanced speech recognition and natural language processing (NLP) to capture and analyze provider–patient co mmunication Identifies clinically relevant information and converts it into standardized AI-generated clinical notes for clinician review. Understands clinical context to create structured documentation, including automated SOAP notes , assessments, treatment plans, and follow-up recommendations. Reduces documentation burden, allowing clinicians to focus on patient-centered interactions and clinical decision-making. How AI Captures Notes Without Disrupting the Visit Step 1 – Ambient listening during the encounter: During the visit, the ambient documentation system securely listens to the conversation between the providers and the patient. Using advanced AI, detect important clinical details while removing unnecessary parts of the discussion. By this, providers can maintain eye contact and engage more naturally with the patient without disturbing the conversation to document information. Step 2 – AI generates a structured SOAP note: Once the conversation is done, the AI gathers the information into clear and structured clinical notes. It creates automated AI SOAP notes, summarizes key findings, documents for clinical assessment, and develops treatment plans based on the discussion. This helps clinicians complete EHR note generation more smoothly while making sure that records remain accurate and consistent. Step 3 – Physician reviews and approves in seconds: Before the information is added to the patient’s chart, the physician reviews the AI-clinical note to verify that it accurately captures the visit. Any important changes can be made quickly, and the note is finalized before entering the EHR. This review step keeps physicians in control of the documentation process while helping maintain clinical accuracy and physician review. Ambient Scribing vs Traditional Transcription: Key Differences Feature Traditional transcription Ambient scribing Documentation timing Created after the patient encounter Created during the patient encounter Process Requires dictation or transcription after the visit Captures information automatically in real time Note Generation Requires manual review and editing Generates structured clinical notes automatically EHR Integration May require additional formatting Can be integrated directly into EHR workflows Administrative Burden Higher due to dictation and editing Lower due to automated documentation Provider Focus More time spent on charting More time spent on patient care AI Medical Scribe Capability Not available Captures, analyzes, and documents encounters automatically Patient Experience Potentially interrupted by note-taking Supports more patient-centered interactions What to Look for in an AI Documentation Tool Not all AI platforms are alike, so healthcare organizations should choose solutions that work well within existing workflows, how precise the clinical output is, how easy it is to use, and the security of data. The right solution can enhance day-to-day efficiency while making a more supportive experience for clinicians. An important factor is how smoothly the tool integrates with current EHR workflows. The strongest solution allows providers to create notes within EHR, by removing the need to switch between multiple systems. This helps in reducing interruptions during clinical practice. Accuracy is equally important, providers need to trust that AI clinical notes truly reflect the patient encounter and clinical decision-making process. A solid physician review and validation process also contributes to maintaining quality, safety, and compliance. Security and compliance should remain key priorities, with organizations making sure that patient data is secured through HIPAA-compliant safeguards and secure access controls. Eventually, the right solution should improve efficiency without complicating workflows or increasing the administrative load on clinicians. How cirrusAI Notes Works Inside CareCloud’s EHR CareCloud’s cirrusAI platform brings ambient clinical documentation directly into the provider workflow through cirrusAI Notes. Rather than requiring physicians to move between different applications, it functions within the CareCloud ecosystem to streamline documentation from start to finish. During the patient visit, cirrusAI Notes records important clinical information and automatically turns it into structured documentation. Providers receive clear, well-organized notes that fit naturally into their clinical workflow and can be quickly reviewed before finalizing. Because cirrusAI in CareCloud’s EHR environment is fully embedded, providers can move from patient interaction to completed documentation more effictively, with less friction and fewer steps. This helps to minimize interruptions and creates a smoother, more efficient workflow throughout the day. Most importantly, cirrusAI Notes save 20% of documentation time per day, giving physicians back valuable hours they can use for patient care, practice growth, or better work-life balance. By minimizing administrative work, CareCloud supports higher provider satisfaction and better overall practice performance. Frequently Asked Questions 1: Is ambient AI documentation HIPAA compliant? Yes, Ambient AI documentation is designed to support HIPAA compliance through safeguards of data, access control, activity logs , and protected storage. H ealthcare organizations should make sure that any solution they implement fulfills HIPAA requirements and aligns with their internal security and compliance standards before integration. 2: Does the AI work for all specialties? Most modern ambient documentation platforms cover an extensiv e range of medical specialties, which includes primary care, internal medicine, cardiology, orthopedics, pediatrics, and others. However, its performance can depend on speci alized medical terminology, so organizations should assess how well a solution fits their unique clinical workflows and documentation requirements. 3: How Valid are AI-generated clinical notes? AI-generated clinical notes can be highly accurate when they are trained in medical language and real clinical workflows. Yet , physician review is still an important step . Ambient documentation tools help make the note-taking process faster, but providers are ultimately responsible for checking the information and making sure it is right before it is added to the official medical record . 4: Can the physician review and edit the note before it is uploaded to the EHR? Yes . Ambient clinical documentation systems are built with physician oversight at the center. Providers can review, edit, and finalize notes b efore they are saved to the EHR. This allows c l inicians to modify d etails , ad d context that is missing , and make sure the documentation truly reflects the patient’s encounter and clinical decisions. title: VSE Corporation Announces Second Quarter 2026 Results
summary: Record Revenue and Profitability Raises 2026 Guidance MIRAMAR, Fla.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- VSE Corporation (“VSE” or the “Company”)…...
body_text: VSE Corporation Announces Second Quarter 2026 Results August 05, 2026 4:15pm EDT Download as PDF Record Revenue and Profitability Raises 2026 Guidance MIRAMAR, Fla.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- VSE Corporation (“VSE” or the “Company”) (NASDAQ: VSEC, VSECU), a leading provider of aviation aftermarket distribution and repair services, announced today results for the second quarter 2026. SECOND QUARTER 2026 RESULTS(1) (As compared to the Second Quarter 2025) Total Revenues of $449.1 million increased 65.0% GAAP Net Income of $28.5 million increased 109.1% GAAP Net Income Margin of 6.4% increased approximately 140 basis points GAAP EPS (Diluted) of $0.91 increased 37.9% Adjusted EBITDA(2) of $86.0 million increased 98.0% Adjusted EBITDA Margin(2) of 19.2% increased approximately 320 basis points Adjusted Net Income(2) of $55.0 million increased 101.2% Adjusted EPS (Diluted)(2) of $1.75 increased 32.6% 1 All numbers reflect results from continuing operations 2 Non-GAAP measures, which reflect a change in the definition of Adjusted Net Income and Adjusted EPS (Diluted). See additional information within this release regarding non-GAAP financial measures MANAGEMENT COMMENTARY “The second quarter marked a defining step forward for VSE as we completed the largest acquisition in our history and established a differentiated global aviation aftermarket platform,” said John Cuomo, President and Chief Executive Officer of VSE Corporation. “With our recent acquisitions of Precision Aviation Group ("PAG") and NorthStar Technologies ("NorthStar"), along with our legacy VSE Aviation businesses, we are positioning VSE to become the world’s leading independent provider of aftermarket distribution and repair services, while remaining firmly grounded in the OEM-centric strategy that has guided our transformation. “The power of the combined platform is already evident in our financial performance. We delivered record revenue and profitability in the second quarter, exceeding our prior expectations and representing a significant step toward achieving a consolidated Adjusted EBITDA margin(2) of more than 20% in the near future. Organic growth remained broad-based, supported by new business wins, expanded capabilities, market share gains, greater share of wallet on existing programs and continued strength across the aviation aftermarket. “Integration is a core VSE capability and an important competitive differentiator. In the short time since closing on the PAG and NorthStar acquisitions, our teams have established clear business and integration plans and are already advancing tangible revenue and margin opportunities, including insourcing, joint sales initiatives, sales-channel alignment and operating efficiencies. We are confident in the combined strength of this platform. As integration progresses, we see meaningful synergy and margin expansion potential, further reinforcing our long-term growth strategy. The strength of our first-half performance, together with our visibility into the remainder of the year, supports our decision to raise both revenue and Adjusted EBITDA margin(2) guidance for 2026,” concluded Mr. Cuomo. “VSE’s second quarter results reflect strong execution and operational discipline across the combined business,” said Adam Cohn, Chief Financial Officer of VSE Corporation. “In the second quarter and compared to the same period last year, revenue increased 65% to $449 million, net income from continuing operations increased 109% to $29 million, Adjusted EBITDA from continuing operations(2) nearly doubled to $86 million, and Adjusted EBITDA margin from continuing operations(2) expanded approximately 320 basis points to a record 19.2%. We generated approximately $28 million of operating cash flow and $19 million of free cash flow(2) in the second quarter, with an Adjusted Net Leverage(2) ratio of approximately 2.4x. In addition, we expect stronger free cash flow(2) generation in the second half of the year, providing increased financial flexibility as we execute our integration priorities and disciplined capital allocation strategy.” SECOND QUARTER HIGHLIGHTS PAG ACQUISITION VSE completed its acquisition of PAG from GenNx360 Capital Partners on May 5, 2026, in a transaction valued at approximately $2.025 billion in cash and equity, the largest acquisition in VSE’s history. The addition of PAG materially expands VSE’s scale, global reach, proprietary content and repair capabilities across commercial, business and general aviation, rotorcraft, OEM and defense end markets. Integration is underway with clear workstreams focused on sales-channel alignment, systems, insourcing, joint commercial opportunities and other revenue and margin synergies across the combined platform. NORTHSTAR ACQUISITION VSE completed its acquisition of NorthStar on April 1, 2026, adding engine-related maintenance, repair and overhaul (“MRO”), third-party logistics and engine component support to the Company’s aftermarket offering. NorthStar’s engine teardown, kitting and engine component-level service capabilities span multiple engine platforms and deepen VSE’s integration within OEM aftermarket supply chains. Since closing, VSE has rebranded the business as VSE Aviation Services, aligned its leadership structure and begun executing initiatives to expand its logistics and MRO capabilities. SECOND QUARTER RESULTS The Company's revenue increased 65.0% year-over-year to a record $449.1 million in the second quarter of 2026. Organic revenue growth was approximately 14%, driven by strength in the commercial engine aftermarket, new business wins, execution on new distribution agreements, expanded product and repair capabilities, market share gains and increased share of wallet on existing programs. The PAG, Aero 3, and NorthStar acquisitions also contributed to the year-over-year increase. Repair and distribution revenue increased 149.4% and 17.2%, respectively, versus the prior-year period. The Company reported net income from continuing operations of $28.5 million, compared to $13.6 million in the second quarter of 2025. Adjusted EBITDA from continuing operations(2) increased by 98.0% to a record $86.0 million, compared to $43.5 million in the prior-year period. Adjusted EBITDA margin from continuing operations(2) reached a record 19.2%, an increase of approximately 320 basis points, driven primarily by a greater mix of higher-margin product and repair activity, continued synergy realization from previously acquired businesses, and contributions from PAG. FINANCIAL RESOURCES AND LIQUIDITY The Company generated $27.6 million of operating cash flow and $18.7 million of free cash flow(2) in the second quarter of 2026. As of June 30, 2026, the Company had $75.4 million in cash and approximately $500.0 million available under its revolving credit facility. Total debt outstanding was $966.7 million. Total net debt(2) was $871.6 million and Adjusted net leverage(2) was approximately 2.4x at quarter end. The Company anticipates stronger free cash flow(2) generation in the second half of 2026, supporting continued deleveraging and disciplined investment in organic and inorganic growth opportunities. UPDATED FULL YEAR 2026 CONSOLIDATED GUIDANCE REVENUE VSE is increasing its full year 2026 revenue guidance based on strong first-half performance, continued organic growth, and improved visibility into the second half of 2026. The Company is also encouraged by the demand environment and customer activity, reinforcing confidence in the strength and durability of the business. The Company now expects full year 2026 revenue growth of 61% to 64%, compared to its prior outlook of 57% to 61%. ADJUSTED EBITDA MARGIN VSE is also increasing its full year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA margin(2) outlook based on record first-half profitability, continued operating execution, and the early benefits of integrating its recent acquisitions. The Company now expects full-year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA margin(2) in the range of 18.7% to 19.0%, compared to its prior outlook of 18.1% to 18.5%. 2 Non-GAAP measures. See additional information at the end of this release regarding non-GAAP financial measures and the Company's inability to provide quantitative reconciliation of forward-looking Adjusted EBITDA to net income. SECOND QUARTER RESULTS Three months ended June 30, Six months ended June 30, (in thousands, except per share data) 2026 2025 % Change 2026 2025 % Change Revenues $ 449,137 $ 272,139 65.0 % $ 773,717 $ 528,184 46.5 % Operating income $ 48,958 $ 22,513 117.5 % $ 81,706 $ 47,017 73.8 % Net income from continuing operations $ 28,523 $ 13,638 109.1 % $ 57,578 $ 27,606 108.6 % EPS (Diluted) $ 0.91 $ 0.66 37.9 % $ 1.94 $ 1.33 45.9 % NON-GAAP MEASURES In addition to the financial measures prepared in accordance with U.S. Generally Accepted Accounting Principles ("GAAP"), this earnings release also contains non-GAAP financial measures. These measures provide useful information to investors. VSE considers Adjusted Net Income from Continuing Operations, Adjusted EPS (Diluted) from Continuing Operations, EBITDA from Continuing Operations, Adjusted EBITDA from Continuing Operations, Adjusted EBITDA margin from continuing operations, Acquisition Adjusted EBITDA from Continuing Operations, TTM Adjusted EBITDA from Continuing Operations, TTM Acquisition Adjusted EBITDA from Continuing Operations, net debt, net leverage ratio, adjusted net leverage ratio, and free cash flow as non-GAAP financial measures and important indicators of performance and useful metrics for management and investors to evaluate VSE’s business's ongoing operating performance on a consistent basis across reporting periods. These non-GAAP financial measures, however, should not be considered in isolation or as a substitute for performance measures prepared in accordance with GAAP. Adjusted Net Income from Continuing Operations represents Net Income adjusted for acquisition-related costs, amortization of intangible assets, stock-based compensation, other discrete items, and related tax impact. Management believes these acquisition-related costs and other discrete items provide useful information about nonrecurring costs and benefits to help users meaningfully evaluate and compare the Company's quarterly and year-to-date performance against prior periods. Adjusted EPS (Diluted) from Continuing Operations is computed by dividing net income, adjusted for the discrete items as identified above and the related tax impacts, by the diluted weighted average number of common shares outstanding. Beginning with the second quarter of 2026, Adjusted Net Income from Continuing Operations and Adjusted EPS (Diluted) from Continuing Operations now include adjustments for amortization of intangible assets and stock-based compensation, with retrospective adjustments included for prior periods presented. Management believes these adjustments provide useful information to evaluate VSE's ongoing operating performance on a consistent basis. EBITDA from Continuing Operations represents net income before interest expense, income taxes, amortization of intangible assets and depreciation and other amortization. Management believes EBITDA from Continuing Operations provides useful information about the Company's operating performance as it isolates non-cash depreciation and amortization charges as well as interest expense and income taxes, which are non-operating items. Adjusted EBITDA from Continuing Operations represents EBITDA from Continuing Operations (as defined above) adjusted for non-cash stock-based compensation and discrete items as identified above. Adjusted EBITDA margin from Continuing Operations represents Adjusted EBITDA from Continuing Operations as a percentage of revenue. Acquisition Adjusted EBITDA from Continuing Operations represents Adjusted EBITDA from Continuing Operations plus the pre-acquisition portion of EBITDA from Continuing Operations for the trailing twelve months. TTM Adjusted EBITDA from Continuing Operations represents Adjusted EBITDA from Continuing Operations as defined above for the trailing twelve months. TTM Acquisition Adjusted EBITDA from Continuing Operations includes pre-acquisition portion of EBITDA from Continuing Operations for the trailing twelve months that is not included in historical results. TTM Acquisition Adjusted EBITDA from Continuing Operations does not reflect all adjustments that would otherwise be required in connection with the preparation of pro forma financial statements in accordance with Article 11 of Regulation S-X. Net debt is defined as principal amount of debt less debt issuance costs and less cash and cash equivalents. Free cash flow represents operating cash flow less capital expenditures. Capital expenditures include purchases of property and equipment. Net leverage ratio is calculated as net debt divided by TTM Adjusted EBITDA from Continuing Operations. Adjusted Net leverage ratio is calculated as net debt divided by TTM Acquisition Adjusted EBITDA from Continuing Operations. Additionally, Adjusted EBITDA margin is also presented as a forward-looking non-GAAP financial measure, defined as estimated operating income before depreciation and amortization expenses as a percentage of revenue. This measure is based solely on information available to VSE as of the date of this earnings release and may differ materially from VSE’s actual operating results as a result of developments that occur after the date of this earnings release. The determination of the amounts that are excluded from this non-GAAP financial measure is a matter of management judgment and depends upon, among other factors, the nature of the underlying expense, income amounts or anticipated synergies recognized in a given period. VSE is unable to present a quantitative reconciliation of forward-looking VSE Adjusted EBITDA from Continuing Operations to net income because certain information regarding the Company’s provision for income taxes is not available, and management cannot reliably predict all of the necessary components of net income at this time without unreasonable effort or expense. For the same reasons, the Company is unable to address the probable significance of the unavailable information. The unavailable information could have a significant impact on the Company’s future financial results. title: Safe Driving Habits That Build a New Driver's Confidence
summary: Enjoy and learn from Life360's blog archive, focused on user life stories and experiences with our premier family safety app.
body_text: White knuckles on the wheel. A death grip at ten and two. That racing heart every time a merge lane shows up out of nowhere. If that's what the first few months behind the wheel feel like, here's the good news: that's not a personality flaw. It's a skill you haven't built yet. Confident drivers aren't born that way, they're made, one green light and one parallel park at a time. And the research backs this up: the more in control a driver feels, the safer they drive. Nervous drivers overcorrect, freeze, or hesitate at the wrong moment. Confident ones scan, plan, and react. So building confidence isn't a nice-to-have on the way to becoming a safe driver, it is becoming a safe driver. This guide breaks down how that confidence gets built: the habits that make driving feel automatic instead of overwhelming, how to practice them the right way, and how families can back a new driver up without hovering. Every drive is practice. Life360 helps you see how it's going. Driving reports that show speed, braking, and phone use turn guesswork into real feedback — so you can coach, not just worry. See Life360 plans Why new drivers feel anxious behind the wheel Driving anxiety is one of the most common, and most normal, parts of learning to drive. Nearly everyone feels it: the tight chest before merging onto the highway, the second-guessing at a four-way stop, the “did I check my blind spot enough” loop that plays on repeat. It happens because driving asks a brand-new driving brain to do a lot at once, track speed, distance, other drivers, signs, and a dozen split-second decisions, all while nothing about it feels automatic yet. That's not a warning sign. It's what it feels like before a skill becomes second nature. The fix isn't “just relax.” It's repetition. Every calm, low-stakes drive teaches the nervous system that this is safe, survivable, even boring. Overcoming driving anxiety isn't about willpower, it's about mileage. Safe driving habits that stick The habits below are the ones that separate a driver who's following rules from one who's in control. Master these, and the rest of driving starts to feel manageable. Scan ahead, not in front. Look 10–15 seconds down the road, not at the bumper ahead. Spotting a slowing car or a merging truck early means reacting with time to spare instead of slamming the brakes. Keep a following distance you can stop in. The three-second rule is the floor, not the goal, leave more space in rain, at night, or in heavy traffic. Manage speed and brake smoothly. Jerky braking is a symptom of reacting too late. Smooth stops mean you saw it coming. Put the phone away, really away. Not on the seat, not face-up on the dash. Distraction doesn't feel dangerous until the one second it is. Check mirrors and blind spots like it's muscle memory. A glance before every lane change, every merge, every turn until it happens without thinking. Adjust for weather and darkness. Rain, fog, and nighttime all shrink the margin for error. (More on driving in tough conditions in our seasonal driving guides.) None of these are complicated. What makes them “stick” is doing them the same way, every single time, until they stop requiring conscious effort. How to practice until the habits are automatic Confidence doesn't come from one big lesson, it comes from stacking small wins. Start small and build up. Empty parking lots first. Then quiet residential streets. Then busier roads. Then, eventually, the highway. Skipping steps is how nerves turn into real problems; taking them in order is how new driver tips translate into new driver habits. Practice often, not forever. A focused 20-minute drive beats a white-knuckled two-hour one. Short, frequent sessions build comfort faster than occasional marathons and they're a lot less exhausting for everyone in the car. Repeat the boring stuff on purpose. Merging, parallel parking, left turns across traffic, the maneuvers that feel hardest are the ones worth practicing until they feel routine. Confidence isn't a light switch. It's a curve, and every low-key drive to the grocery store moves it forward. It's also worth the effort: Life360 data shows crash rates climb sharply between ages 17 and 20 , which makes this window — the one full of empty-lot laps and quiet-street practice — the one that matters most. How modern vehicle safety features build confidence New drivers today have a real advantage: modern vehicle safety technology that acts like a second set of eyes. Features like automatic emergency braking, blind-spot monitoring, and lane-keep assist are built to catch the moments a still-developing driver might miss, a car hidden in a blind spot, a sudden stop ahead, a gentle drift out of a lane. The key is framing these features the right way: as support, not a substitute for attention. They're a safety net, not an autopilot. The driver is still the one scanning ahead, checking mirrors, and making the call, the technology backs them up when it matters most. Choosing a vehicle with this kind of safety-first technology, and understanding how to use it, is one more way new drivers can drive with real, earned confidence instead of white-knuckle hope. How families can support a new driver Confidence doesn't get built solo, it gets built with backup. The most useful thing a parent or partner can do is trade criticism for encouragement. “You handled that merge well” lands a lot better than a running list of everything done wrong, and it's more likely to make the next drive better too. Reviewing a driving session together, calmly, after the fact, not mid-turn, turns mistakes into lessons instead of moments of panic. That's where a tool like Life360 earns its keep: driving reports that show speed, braking, and phone use turn “how was the drive?” into an actual conversation instead of a guessing game, and arrival check-ins mean nobody has to send (or receive) an anxious “did you make it?” text. Peace of mind for the driver, and for everyone waiting to hear they got there safe. (See our full guide to driving safety features at /driving-safety for more.) Skip the anxious "did you make it?" text. Just know. Life360 sends an arrival alert the moment they pull in — so you're not staring at your phone waiting, and they're not distracted replying. See Life360 plans Signs a new driver is ready to drive solo There's no single test for “ready” but there are signs worth watching for: Judgment under pressure. Do they make the safe call even when no one's watching? Comfort. Can they hold a conversation without losing focus on the road? Consistent rule-following. Signals, speed limits, full stops, every time, not when it's convenient. Earned trust. Has a track record of calm, low-drama drives started to build up? When those boxes start checking themselves off, solo driving stops being a leap of faith and starts being the next logical step. Confidence, built one drive at a time Nobody feels like a confident driver on day one and that's the point. Confidence isn't the starting line, it's what shows up after enough calm, deliberate practice that the habits stop needing conscious thought. Scan ahead, keep space, put the phone away, check the mirrors, do that consistently, and the nerves fade a lot faster than most new drivers expect. None of it has to happen alone. Whether it's a parent riding shotgun, honest feedback after a drive, or the kind of vehicle safety tech that backs up a still-developing driver, support makes the curve shorter. Every low-key trip to the store is one more rep and one more sign that a nervous new driver is becoming a genuinely safe one. FAQ How do I become a more confident driver? Confidence comes from repetition, not luck. Practice regularly in low-stakes settings, empty lots, quiet streets, before working up to busier roads. Each calm, successful drive teaches your brain that driving is manageable, and that sense of control builds real confidence over time. How long does it take to feel confident driving? It varies, but most new drivers start feeling noticeably more comfortable after a few months of regular practice. Confidence builds fastest with frequent, short drives rather than occasional long ones — consistency matters more than total hours behind the wheel. How do I overcome driving anxiety? Start with low-pressure practice: empty parking lots, familiar routes, daylight hours. Anxiety fades as your brain logs enough safe, uneventful drives to realize there's nothing to fear. Avoid jumping straight into high-stress driving like highways or rush hour before you're ready. What are the most important safe driving habits? Scanning ahead, keeping a safe following distance, avoiding phone distractions, and checking mirrors and blind spots before every lane change. These habits, done consistently, prevent the vast majority of avoidable accidents and they're the foundation everything else builds on. The habits take time. The safety net doesn't have to wait. Real-time location, driving reports, and arrival alerts — Life360 keeps the whole family connected while a new driver finds their confidence. See Life360 plans

title: Kyivstar and Ukrtelecom Launch Open Access Partnership to Accelerate Fiber Broadband Expansion in Ukraine
summary: The Open Access partnership enables reciprocal use of both operators’ fiber networks, accelerating broadband expansion and modern digital services for millions of Ukrainians. KYIV, Ukraine, August 17, 2026 - Kyivstar Group Ltd. (“Kyivstar”) (Nasdaq: KYIV; KYIVW), the parent company of JSC Kyivstar,
body_text: Kyivstar and Ukrtelecom Launch Open Access Partnership to Accelerate Fiber Broadband Expansion in Ukraine 17.08.2026 PDF Version The Open Access partnership enables reciprocal use of both operators’ fiber networks, accelerating broadband expansion and modern digital services for millions of Ukrainians. KYIV, Ukraine, August 17, 2026 - Kyivstar Group Ltd. (“Kyivstar”) (Nasdaq: KYIV; KYIVW), the parent company of JSC Kyivstar, Ukraine’s leading digital operator and part of VEON Group (Nasdaq: VEON), announced that JSC Kyivstar and JSC Ukrtelecom have signed an agreement to cooperate under an Open Access model, based on the shared use of telecommunications infrastructure. Under the project, both operators will reciprocally use parts of each other's networks, helping bring fiber coverage to homes across the country quickly and efficiently. As part of the project, Kyivstar will provide Home Internet services and access to its digital ecosystem by using Ukrtelecom’s GPON network, while Ukrtelecom will provide Optical Internet services by using Kyivstar’s extensive fiber network on an open market basis. The Open Access model provides network access on transparent and non-discriminatory terms. According to the FTTH Council Europe, this approach promotes fair and transparent competition among service providers. The implementation of the project will contribute to the further development of Ukraine’s telecommunications market while also enabling faster expansion of access to fiber broadband and modern digital services for a greater number of Ukrainians. “Open Access gives us a practical way to make better use of the infrastructure we’ve already built, while accelerating the rollout of modern digital services,” commented Yurii Kurmaz, CEO of Ukrtelecom, on the launch of the partnership. “We believe this model will become one of the key drivers behind the next stage of growth in Ukraine’s telecoms sector. With 95,000 kilometers of existing fiber network, Ukrtelecom is ready to scale this approach and open up new opportunities for modern telecommunications services across the country.” Each operator retains its direct relationship with its subscribers by independently defining its tariff policy and commercial terms, while also providing customer support and billing. The owner of the network remains responsible for its operation and technical maintenance. Information exchanged between the companies is limited to the technical data required to provide network access as part of the project. “This Open Access partnership is an important milestone in expanding Ukraine’s digital infrastructure. It lets us reach far more customers with high-quality fiber broadband, while making efficient of the networks we already have in place,” said Oleksandr Komarov, CEO of Kyivstar. “For our customers, this means greater opportunities to benefit from Kyivstar Home Internet services and Kyivstar’s digital ecosystem, including converged offerings that combine mobile communications, home internet and television services within a single package. Through this partnership, these opportunities will become available to an even greater number of Ukrainians.” The first phase of the project, during which the companies will validate the cooperation model and the operation of the information systems integrated as part of the project, will begin in the Odesa, Vinnytsia and Kirovohrad regions and will cover more than one million residents of Ukraine. The geographical scope of the partnership is expected to expand to other regions of Ukraine in subsequent phases, with further announcements to follow. About Kyivstar Group Ltd. Kyivstar Group Ltd. is a Nasdaq-listed holding company that operates Kyivstar, Ukraine’s leading digital operator and the first Ukrainian company to list on a U.S. stock exchange. Kyivstar Group Ltd.’s companies provide a broad range of connectivity and digital services, including mobile and fixed-line voice and data, ride-hailing, e-health, digital TV, and enterprise solutions such as Big Data, cloud, and cybersecurity. For more information, please visit https://investors.kyivstar.ua . Nasdaq tickers: KYIV; KYIVW About JSC Kyivstar JSC Kyivstar is Ukraine’s leading digital operator, serving more than 21,8 million mobile customers and over 1.3 million home internet fixed line customers as of June 30, 2026. The company provides services using a wide range of mobile and fixed technologies, including 4G, Big Data, cloud solutions, cybersecurity services, digital TV, and more. JSC Kyivstar is wholly owned by Kyivstar Group Ltd. (Nasdaq: KYIV; KYIVW), whose shares are traded on the U.S. stock exchange Nasdaq. Additional information: pr@kyivstar.net , www.kyivstar.ua . About JSC Ukrtelecom JSC Ukrtelecom is Ukraine’s leading fixed-line telecommunications operator and the owner of the country’s largest GPON infrastructure. title: Dental Practice Management Software: The $4B Market Reshaping Dentistry
summary: The dental PMS market hits $1.97B in 2026 and is headed to $4.16B by 2035. Learn which features drive ROI, top platforms, and how AI extends your PMS capabilities.
body_text: Why Dental Practice Management Software Is the Backbone of Modern Dentistry Running a dental practice in 2026 without robust practice management software is like performing a root canal without an X-ray — technically possible, but unnecessarily painful and prone to costly mistakes. From scheduling and billing to insurance verification and patient communication, practice management software (PMS) has become the operational nervous system of every high-performing dental office. The numbers back this up. According to Towards Healthcare , the global dental practice management software market was valued at USD 1.97 billion in 2026 and is projected to reach approximately USD 4.16 billion by 2035 , expanding at a CAGR of 8.64%. That's not a niche technology trend — it's a fundamental shift in how dental practices operate. Whether you're a solo practitioner trying to compete with DSOs, an office manager drowning in administrative tasks, or a group practice operator looking to standardize workflows across locations, understanding the PMS landscape is essential. This guide breaks down what's driving the market, which features matter most, how to calculate ROI, and how AI tools are extending what PMS platforms can do. The State of the Dental PMS Market in 2026 A Multi-Billion Dollar Industry With Serious Momentum The dental PMS market isn't just growing — it's accelerating. The Yahoo Finance market report highlights a competitive landscape where both established players and emerging AI-native platforms are vying for market share. What's fueling this growth? A combination of aging populations requiring more dental care, rising patient expectations for digital-first experiences, and the relentless pressure on practices to do more with less staff. North America leads the charge. According to Patientdesk.ai's 2026 market analysis , North America dominates the dental PMS market with a 41% share in 2026 , driven by advanced healthcare IT infrastructure and high adoption of digital dental workflows. European markets are catching up quickly, particularly in the UK and Germany where national health systems are pushing digital transformation. Solo Practices Are Driving Adoption One of the most surprising findings in recent market data is who's actually buying PMS software. According to Clerri's comprehensive statistics report , solo practices hold a 59.29% market share in 2026 . This confirms that independent dentists — not just large DSOs — are investing heavily in technology to stay competitive. This makes sense when you think about it. A solo practitioner with one or two front-desk staff members has the most to gain from automation. Every hour saved on manual scheduling, insurance verification, or billing follow-up is an hour that can be redirected toward patient care or practice growth. Cloud vs. On-Premise: The Deployment Shift The way practices deploy their PMS is changing rapidly. Towards Healthcare reports that the web-based deployment segment dominated the dental PMS market with a 46% share in 2025 , and the cloud-based segment is expected to grow at the fastest CAGR going forward. The reasons are straightforward: cloud-based systems offer lower upfront costs, automatic updates, remote access, and easier multi-location management — all critical advantages for modern practices. The market is also shifting from monolithic platforms to modular ecosystems. The pureplay PMS segment dominated with a 68% share in 2025, but dental PMS add-ons are expected to grow at the fastest CAGR — signaling that practices increasingly want best-of-breed tools that integrate with their core system rather than a single platform that does everything adequately. Core Features That Define a High-Performance PMS Scheduling, Reminders, and Patient Communication At its most basic level, a dental PMS manages your schedule. But the best platforms in 2026 go far beyond a digital appointment book. They send automated reminders via text, email, and voice; manage recall and reactivation campaigns; and flag scheduling gaps before they become lost revenue. This matters enormously because no-shows cost the healthcare industry an estimated $150 billion annually . Even modest PMS-driven improvements in reminder effectiveness can recapture thousands of dollars in lost production each month for a typical dental practice. A system that automatically sends a reminder three days out, a text the morning of the appointment, and a follow-up for rescheduling if the patient cancels can dramatically move the needle on your show rate. Insurance Verification and Billing Automation Insurance billing is where most practices hemorrhage money — and where a great PMS pays for itself fastest. Manual insurance verification is time-consuming, error-prone, and a leading cause of claim denials. Modern PMS platforms automate eligibility checks, flag coverage issues before the patient arrives, and submit clean claims electronically. The financial impact is substantial. According to CertifyHealth's complete guide to practice management software , practices using integrated PMS cut their admin cost per visit by an average of 21% in the first year . More dramatically, cutting claim denial rates from 12% to 4% on $2 million in claims can recover $160,000 per year — money that was previously being left on the table due to avoidable billing errors. Reporting, Analytics, and Practice Intelligence The third pillar of a high-performance PMS is data visibility. The best platforms give practice owners and office managers real-time dashboards showing production by provider, collection rates, treatment acceptance rates, new patient trends, and recall effectiveness. Without this data, you're flying blind — making staffing, marketing, and investment decisions based on gut feel rather than evidence. Look for PMS platforms that offer customizable reports, benchmarking against industry averages, and the ability to drill down from practice-level metrics to individual provider or operatory performance. The ROI Case: What Practices Actually Gain From PMS Investment Payback Periods That Surprise Most Owners One of the most common objections to investing in a new or upgraded PMS is cost. But the ROI data is compelling. According to CertifyHealth , most practices earn back their PMS investment in 4–6 months , with total annual savings from reduced denials, fewer no-shows, and less manual work potentially exceeding $268,000 per year for a mid-sized practice. That's not a theoretical projection — it's based on documented outcomes from practices that have made the switch. The savings come from multiple sources: fewer denied claims, reduced administrative labor hours, better recall rates, and improved treatment plan acceptance when patients receive timely follow-up. Real-World Case Study: ROOT Periodontics The numbers become even more concrete when you look at specific practice outcomes. According to Clerri's statistics report , ROOT Periodontics achieved a 35% increase in gross production and a 29% increase in new patient acquisition after implementing comprehensive practice management software. These aren't marginal improvements — they represent a fundamental transformation in how the practice operates and grows. The Administrative Burden Reduction Beyond the financial metrics, there's a quality-of-life dimension to PMS ROI that often gets overlooked. Market.us Media reports that dental PMS implementation results in a notable 50% reduction in administrative tasks , with approximately 85% of patients reporting a positive experience with digitally-enabled practices. When your front desk team spends less time on manual data entry, phone tag, and paper-based processes, they can focus on what actually matters: creating exceptional patient experiences that drive loyalty and referrals. AI-Powered Automation: The Defining Trend of 2026 From Feature Lists to Intelligent Workflows The conversation around dental PMS has shifted dramatically in 2026. It's no longer about which platform has the longest feature list — it's about which systems can intelligently automate the right workflows at the right time. "The best dental practice management software in 2026 isn't about doing more. It's about doing the right things automatically." — Solutionreach According to Open Loop Health's analysis of top dental trends , AI-powered automation is the defining trend in practice management software for 2026. Systems now automate insurance verification and billing, patient communication workflows, and appointment scheduling and reminders — with the American Medical Association noting that reducing administrative burdens is the greatest use of AI for physicians . This isn't just about efficiency. It's about consistency. An AI-powered system sends the right message to the right patient at the right time, every single time — without relying on a staff member to remember, prioritize, or execute the task manually. Where AI Adds the Most Value in PMS Workflows The highest-impact AI applications within and alongside dental PMS platforms include: Automated appointment reminders and confirmations that adapt based on patient response behavior Intelligent recall campaigns that identify lapsed patients and trigger personalized outreach Real-time insurance eligibility verification that flags issues before the patient arrives Smart billing workflows that predict denial risk and route claims accordingly Treatment plan follow-up that nurtures patients who didn't schedule after a consultation Extending Your PMS With AI Layers Here's an important nuance: even the best PMS platforms have gaps. They're excellent at managing data and workflows within the practice, but they often fall short on 24/7 patient-facing interactions — after-hours calls, real-time chat, and proactive outreach at scale. This is where AI tools that integrate with your existing PMS become powerful force multipliers. Patientdesk.ai integrates directly with leading platforms including Dentrix, Open Dental, Eaglesoft, and more , layering AI-powered receptionist capabilities on top of your existing system without requiring you to rip and replace your current PMS. Patients can book appointments at 2 AM, get their questions answered instantly, and receive personalized follow-up — all while your PMS continues to manage the underlying data and workflows. Leading Dental PMS Platforms: What to Know in 2026 Open Dental: Best Overall for Independent Practices For general practices and small groups that want highly customizable, cost-controlled software with full data ownership, Open Dental remains the top-rated option. It holds a 4.6/5 rating as of January 2026 and starts at $179/month per location , making it one of the most accessible enterprise-grade options on the market. Its open-source architecture means it integrates with a wide ecosystem of third-party tools, giving practices flexibility as their needs evolve. Dentrix and Eaglesoft: The Established Enterprise Players Dentrix (Henry Schein) and Eaglesoft (Patterson Dental) remain dominant in the mid-to-large practice segment, particularly among practices that purchase equipment and supplies through their respective parent companies. Both offer comprehensive feature sets, strong support networks, and deep integration with imaging and clinical documentation tools. The tradeoff is typically higher cost and less flexibility compared to open-source alternatives. Curve Dental and Denticon: Cloud-Native Options for Growing Groups For practices prioritizing cloud-native architecture and multi-location management, Curve Dental and Denticon (Planet DDS) are strong contenders. Both were built from the ground up for web-based deployment, offering true anywhere-access and streamlined multi-site reporting — critical capabilities for DSOs and group practices managing multiple locations. Choosing the Right Platform for Your Practice Type The right PMS depends heavily on your practice type, growth trajectory, and existing technology stack. Key questions to ask: Solo vs. group: Do you need multi-location management and consolidated reporting? Cloud vs. on-premise: Are you comfortable with subscription pricing and internet-dependent access? Integration needs: Does the platform connect with your imaging software, patient communication tools, and AI add-ons? Data ownership: Who owns your patient data if you switch platforms? Support model: What does implementation, training, and ongoing support look like? Maximizing PMS Value: Beyond the Software Itself Implementation and Training Are Half the Battle The most sophisticated PMS in the world delivers zero ROI if your team doesn't use it correctly. Implementation quality and staff training are consistently cited as the top factors separating practices that see dramatic results from those that feel like they overpaid for a glorified appointment book. Invest in proper onboarding, designate a PMS champion on your team who owns ongoing optimization, and schedule quarterly reviews of your system configuration to ensure you're taking advantage of new features as they're released. Integrating Revenue Recovery Tools A strong PMS handles the operational backbone of your practice, but revenue recovery — particularly around treatment plan follow-up and case acceptance — often requires specialized tools. The Patientdesk.ai AI Patient Sales Coordinator is designed specifically for this gap: automatically following up with patients who received treatment plans but haven't scheduled, nurturing them through personalized outreach until they're ready to commit. When layered on top of a solid PMS, this kind of targeted revenue recovery can meaningfully move your case acceptance rate. Measuring What Matters Once your PMS is fully implemented, establish a baseline for the metrics that matter most: Collection rate (target: 98%+ of adjusted production) Claim denial rate (target: under 5%) No-show/cancellation rate (target: under 8%) New patient acquisition (month-over-month trend) Treatment plan acceptance rate (target: 85%+) Recall effectiveness (percentage of active patients seen in the last 18 months) Review these metrics monthly, and use your PMS reporting tools to identify which workflows are underperforming and where automation can close the gap. The Future of Dental Practice Management Software Predictive Analytics and Proactive Practice Management The next frontier for dental PMS is moving from reactive reporting to predictive intelligence. Rather than telling you what happened last month, next-generation platforms will flag which patients are at risk of lapsing before they do, predict which claims are likely to be denied before you submit them, and recommend schedule optimizations based on historical production patterns. This shift from descriptive to predictive analytics will fundamentally change how practice owners and office managers make decisions — moving from gut-feel management to data-driven precision. The Modular Ecosystem Model As noted earlier, the market is shifting toward modular, integrated ecosystems rather than monolithic platforms. This means your "practice management software" in 2027 and beyond will likely be a curated stack of best-of-breed tools — a core PMS for scheduling and billing, an AI communication layer for patient engagement, a dedicated analytics platform for business intelligence, and specialized tools for imaging, treatment planning, and revenue recovery — all connected through open APIs and real-time data sync. The practices that thrive will be those that build this integrated stack intentionally, choosing tools that work together seamlessly rather than accumulating disconnected point solutions. AI as a Standard Feature, Not a Premium Add-On Perhaps the most significant shift on the horizon is the commoditization of AI within PMS platforms. Features that feel cutting-edge today — automated eligibility verification, intelligent recall campaigns, predictive no-show scoring — will be table stakes within two to three years. The competitive advantage will shift to practices that use AI most effectively, not just those that have it. Key Takeaways for Practice Owners and Office Managers The dental practice management software market is at an inflection point. With the market growing from $1.97 billion to a projected $4.16 billion by 2035, the technology is maturing rapidly — and the gap between practices that leverage it effectively and those that don't is widening. Here's what to take away: Adoption is near-universal — with an approximately 80% adoption rate in the US and Europe, PMS is no longer optional for competitive practices ROI is fast and measurable — most practices recoup their investment in 4–6 months through reduced denials, fewer no-shows, and lower administrative costs Cloud-based and modular architectures are the future — choose platforms that integrate well and give you data ownership AI automation is the defining differentiator — the best PMS platforms in 2026 automate the right workflows, not just more workflows Your PMS is a foundation, not a ceiling — layer AI tools on top to extend capabilities into 24/7 patient engagement, revenue recovery, and proactive outreach The practices winning in 2026 aren't necessarily the ones with the biggest budgets or the most staff — they're the ones that have built smart, integrated technology stacks that let their teams focus on patient care while automation handles the rest.

title: Breast Cancer Risk Checks May Miss 95% of High-Risk Women Under 50, Study Warns
summary: New research highlights gaps in current breast cancer referral guidelines Breast cancer remains one of the most serious health challenges affecting women in the UK, particularly among younger women.
